## Lyric Lab Notebook




An append-only research log. One dated entry per working session: the objective,
what was built, **errors found and their causes**, findings, and how each result
was verified. Newest entries at the top. This is the scientific record — it
should let a later reader reconstruct not just *what* changed but *why*, and
which claims were actually checked against the running system.

Conventions:
- Every capability claim cites how it was verified (test + result), model-free where stated.
- Errors are recorded with their **cause**, not just the fix — a wrong assumption is data.
- "Verified against the real system" means run under `./venv_lyric/bin/python3`, real Postgres, `STRICT_MODEL_FREE` + `assert_model_free` for learning claims.

---

## 2026-11-01 (105) — The reading measure charged the word records for using the senses they were built to hold, and a fifth of the questions could not be read at all: a preposition carried along with the wh-phrase was a thing

**Objective.** *"there was a big fucking issue with lyrics fucking reading responding and understanding. This has
been a four or five day fucking problem."* Account for where reading and responding fail end to end from the runs
already on disk, and fix in order of the counts.

### THE ACCOUNT (10-26, main, the fit half's 231 questions), grouped by what the system itself did

| | n |
|---|---:|
| the reasoner was asked once, took **zero steps**, returned an **empty** answer | **179** |
| the question was read only in part | 19 |
| no reply at all | 4 |
| the reasoner said "not entailed by the premises" (open world, honest) | 4 |
| right | 18 |
| wrong | 5 |

Of the 179, **177 ask a conjunctive pattern with unknowns** (`instance_of(?v0, evolve) & done_by(?v0, ?v1) &
moves_to(?v0, ?v3) ? ?v3`) and 2 are plain yes/no. So "the reasoner is broken" is the wrong reading of it:
`_asked_of_events`/`_held_ways` do solve patterns, and found no way because what reading HELD from the text and what
the question ASKS are not the same facts. Every one of those replies fell through to the recall dump, which is
reached only when nothing answered — so the dump is a symptom, not the defect.

### THE SHAPE THAT DOMINATES WHAT FAILS, AND WHICH THE READING MEASURE CANNOT SEE

**82 of the 456 questions (18%)** carry a preposition along with the wh-phrase ("From which port did the first failed
password come?", 43) or strand one at the end ("What is rain composed of?", 42), and **11 of the 19 read only in
part** are that shape. The grammar said so itself: *"I understood 'which port did the failed password from
123.235.32.19 come', but not how 'From' fits with it."*

(101) measured the same gap from the other side — 22.1% of the gold's categories Lyric cannot express, over half of
it the one decision to have no `pp` — and left it alone because **the PMB's dev split holds the shape once in 911
sentences.** That is right about the PMB and wrong about English: the hand-analysed treebanks hold it 27 times in
EWT's dev, 33 in GUM's dev and 29 in PUD's test. GRAMMAR-01 is blind to a construction that breaks a fifth of what
people ask.

### THE CAUSE, from the grammar, on the same sentence with one thing changed

| read by the grammar built from files | |
|---|---|
| `Does South Asia border East Asia?` | right |
| `What does South Asia border?` | right — the object gap works |
| `What bounds South Asia?` | right |
| `Which port did the password come from?` | **right**: `word_from(?v0, ?v1)` |
| `From which port did the password come?` | **garbage**: `done_by(?v0, from) & instance_of(?v2, "password come")` |

All six of a preposition's categories are a modifier of something beside it (`templates["PREPOSITION"]`) and a
wh-word is neither, so carried to the front it has nothing to take and the cheapest reading left makes it A THING.
In prose the same defect reads `isa(with, premise)`, `isa(from, meal)`, `isa(in, union)`.

Also measured, and worth keeping: the first reading in a process costs **90s** (the rules are built then) and every
reading after it 0.0s, so a probe against the real file-held grammar is cheap once warm. That is what made this
day's twenty-odd probes possible.

### THE FIX: read it as the grammar already reads "where"

"Where" is this construction in one word and the grammar has had it all along (`S[wq].e/S[q].e` with `prep(e, a,
where)` and `asked(a)`). `Lexicon._carried` offers the same for a preposition followed by a wh-word: the wh-phrase's
own gap is dropped, because the preposition's object fills it, and the preposition's link joins the clause's doing to
what the gap stood for. **Only a gap the preposition could fill** — a clause missing a thing to its RIGHT, never a
subject gap ("From which port came it?" is not English). Nothing else about the wh-phrase changes: its category, its
weighing and the rest of its meaning are its own. `From which port did the password come?` now reads fact for fact
what the stranded sentence reads.

### MEASURED

**The measure was corrected first**: a preposition read as one entry with its wh-phrase has no head of its own, and
the analysis joins it to that very wh-word, which `prose_joins` already counts right for a content word inside an
entry of several words. The baseline was re-measured under the corrected measure and did not move (2 of 12 either
way), so the correction does not flatter it.

| held-out hand-analysed sentences that front a preposition | without | with |
|---|---:|---:|
| EWT dev (27 sentences): the preposition joined right | 2 of 12 | **4 of 12** |
| EWT dev: content words joined right | 100 of 166 | 98 of 166 |
| EWT dev: read no whole | 12 of 27 | 12 of 27 |
| PUD test (29 sentences): the preposition joined right | 0 of 20 | **9 of 20** |
| PUD test: content words joined right | 186 of 311 (59.8%) | **191 of 311 (61.4%)** |
| PUD test: read no whole | 8 of 29 | 8 of 29 |
| PUD test: seconds | 298 | 301 |

| the benchmark's own 43 carried questions | without | with |
|---|---:|---:|
| read at all | 31 of 43 | **38 of 43** |
| the preposition not made a thing | 29 | **38** |

**And it costs nothing on the split that scores reading** (`--without-carried`, as `--without-structure` prices the
structure view): GRAMMAR-01, PMB dev, read whole 892 → 893, strict whole right 204 → 206, **senses aside 392 →
397**, facts F1 82.9% → **83.1%**, the one spoken of before unnamed 494 → 499, links by the word's own uses 1,165 of
1,411 → 1,170 of 1,413, read-to-another-meaning 489 → **485**, 466s → 467s. The split holds the construction about
once, so what was asked was whether the rule COSTS anything; five more whole meanings come right instead.

### "WHOM" HAD NO RELATIVE USE AT ALL

Found while reading the 27: `who` has `rel:object` and **"whom" had only `wh:object`**, so a relative clause on the
object's own form — "a partner whom you can trust and with whom you can, together, develop" — could not be read at
all. One entry, mirroring `who`'s exactly. EWT dev: read no whole 12 → **11**, content words joined right 98 of 166
→ **107 of 184**, the preposition 4 of 12 → 5 of 13. PMB dev: every figure identical, so it is free there.
`test_whom_asks_who_a_thing_was_done_to_never_who_did_it` was amended, not weakened — it pinned the whole list of
entries, where what it is for is that none of them takes a SUBJECT gap, and that assertion now fails if one is ever
added.

**ERROR, CORRECTED HERE.** Commits `810f34f3` and this entry's first draft said 110 of 456 questions and 13 of 19. My
count's preposition list was not word-bounded, so "iron?" matched "on" and "group?" matched "up". The figures are 82
and 11.

### THE MEASUREMENT TOOL (101) ASKED FOR IS BUILT

(101): *"Caching the records to disk would make a variant run about a minute... That is the measurement tool this
loop has been missing all day."* It had been written and **never run**, and it crashed one line after writing its own
cache (`say(f"recorded whole {held:,} ...")`, formatting a dict). Fixed; the cache is 6,985 records, 108 MB, ignored
by git, and the records load in **470s** instead of 3,674s, so a variant run is 8.5 minutes, mostly the 440s
teaching phase. `--words-without used_as,means,senses.kind_of,…` holds every record with one layer (or one part of
each of its senses) emptied and the rest as main holds it, each field emptied to a value of its own kind — `used` is
an int, and emptying it to `()` would have made every record unheld while the run reported one field left out.

### THE RECORD LAYER PRICED — AND THE 20 POINTS WERE THE MEASURE, NOT THE READING

**The bisect.** Seven runs, each holding every record with ONE layer emptied and the rest as main holds it:

| without | senses aside: whole right | facts F1 | links by a word's own uses |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `used_as` | 277 | 62.7% | 59.5% |
| `means` | 275 | 62.3% | 58.9% |
| `joins`, `joins_things` | 276 | 62.4% | 59.2% |
| `forms` | 276 | 62.4% | 59.1% |
| **`senses`** | **406** | **83.4%** | **83.5%** |
| `capitalized`, `shapes`, `said_of_doing`, `said_after` | 275 | 62.2% | 59.0% |
| `said_alone`, `used_before_doing`, `used_asking`, `together`, `uses` | 276 | 62.5% | 58.9% |
| (records on, nothing left out) | 273 | 62.3% | 59.0% |

Six layers move two to four sentences. `senses` moves 133 — so the sense layer is the whole of it, and the rest of
the record is a small net gain.

**Then the sense layer, taken apart the same way:** `kind_of` +12, `seen_with` +19, `places` +5, `frames` +3,
`related` 0, and `covers`+`used` **−15** (the usage counts are how a sense is chosen at all). All five of the first
together: senses aside 276 → 297. **No part of a sense accounts for the 133**, which is what sent me to the
sentences.

**THE 133 ARE 129 SENTENCES WITH THE SAME LINKS IN THE SAME PLACES AND ANOTHER WORD FOR THE SAME SENSE.** Of the 138
dev sentences the sense layer alone loses, 129 differ from the gold only in what a thing is called, and every one is
a WordNet synonym of it:

```
Tom waved.       gold instance_of(?v0, wave)     read instance_of(?v0, beckon)
You're vain.     gold has_property(?listener, vain)   read has_property(?listener, conceited)
We buy CDs.      gold instance_of(?v2, cd)       read instance_of(?v2, compact disk)
We concurred.    gold instance_of(?v0, concur)   read instance_of(?v0, agree)
I liked Tony.    gold instance_of(?v0, like)     read instance_of(?v0, desire wish)
```

**The cause, in the measure.** `senses_aside` renames the GOLD by the name the reading gives each word, and it can
only do that where the PMB **anchors** that term to a word (`at`, from the document's concepts' spans). Where the PMB
anchors none — a quality said by a copula, a kind on a line of its own — the gold keeps its own word, and a synonym
the reading chose **from the right sense** is scored as a miss. So the records, whose whole purpose is to give a word
its senses, were charged for using them.

**The fix was written on 10-28 and never called here.** `named_by_their_words` sits in the same file, names both
sides by the word of the sentence a thing is a sense of, and its docstring says `senses_aside` "counted a sense
chosen from what fills a verb's places wrong where the word was read right". `on_store.py` has scored its headline
error budget that way since; `experiment.py` — which produced every figure in (99) through (105) — never used it.
Wired in as a fourth way, applied to the reading and the gold alike.

**Like for like, same code, same split:**

| | records on | records off |
|---|---:|---:|
| strict: whole right | **232 (25.5%)** | 206 (22.6%) |
| strict: facts F1 | **51.7%** | 47.4% |
| senses aside (the old way) | 276 (30.3%) | **397 (43.6%)** |
| senses aside: facts F1 | 62.4% | **83.1%** |
| **by their words: whole right** | **503 (55.2%)** | 488 (53.6%) |
| **by their words: facts F1** | **79.6%** | 79.0% |

**The word records HELP** — +26 whole meanings strict, +15 by their words, better facts F1 both ways. The old measure
said they cost 121 whole meanings and 20.7 points of F1.

**WITHDRAWN.** (101)'s headline — *"the word records fix the sense label and wreck the structure"* — and (100)'s
*"the senses-aside drop cannot be a labelling artefact, by construction"*, and my own statement earlier today that
*"main is paying the 20-point column"*. The structural loss the sense layer really causes is **9 sentences of 911**.
Main needs no change on this account.

**What it cost to find:** (101) spent a day on four fixes aimed at a regression that was not there, and reported them
as net negative against this measure. The lesson is the one (101) itself drew and then applied to the wrong thing:
when a measurement says a layer built to help is hurting, take ONE sentence apart before building anything.

**Reading's honest standing on held-out PMB dev**, with the records as main holds them: **55.2% of whole meanings,
facts F1 79.6%** (strict, every fine-grained sense counted: 25.5%). Against the bar of 95% on whole meanings, and
against the published state of the art on this corpus of 89.3 Counter F1 and Boxer's 74.3 (a different fact measure,
so not directly comparable).

### THE SAMPLE ON MAIN: READING IS BETTER AND ANSWERING DOES NOT RETURN

The owner chose a three-text sample before the two-hour half (texts 1, 47, 50: 15 sentences, 24 questions), on
`lyric_db`, read-only. **It never reached a question.**

**Reading on main, text 1 (South Asia), 10 sentences: 6 read whole** against 7 on 10-26, and the two differ --
"South Asia, with a population of 2.04 billion, contains a quarter (25%) of the world's population." reads whole
now where it read nothing then. The first sentence costs 554s (the rules are built on the first reading, once per
process), the rest 4.7s to 219s, the longest sentences the slowest.

**Then the first question -- "Is South Asia a sub-region of Asia?", the one (103) made answerable -- ran for 16
minutes without returning**, at 95% of a core and 5.4 GB, and was stopped. On `lyric_dev` the same question
answered "Yes." in a moment ((104), reading bypassed). So the cost is main's, not the question's: 24 questions at
that rate is not a two-hour run.

**What the sample is worth:** this is why the owner's rule is a sample first. The 10-26 run answered 231 questions
in 7,398s, about 30s each; whatever has changed since, answering on main is now at least thirty times slower than
that on its first question, and the prose benchmark cannot be run until that is traced. The candidates, in order:
(103)'s renaming lets the reasoner CHAIN where it used to take zero steps, and main's graph is large; the recall
path; `_held_ways` over a large store.

**Nothing was written.** The run's own end-of-run check never ran, so it was checked by hand: 0 rows made in the
last 75 minutes in `unified.concepts`, `beliefs`, `scoped_concept_relations`, `scoped_beliefs`, `experience_pool`,
`memory_media`, `memory_operations`.

### CLOSED BY READING THE CODE, NO RUN

(103) left open that `hold_for_person` has no `remembered()` guard where `hold_scoped_relation` does, so a
`remembers=False` conversation might persist scoped rows on main. **It cannot:** `ScopedContextStore.observe` writes
only through `hold_scoped_relation` and `_observe_belief` → `hold_scoped_belief`, both of which hold in working
memory when nothing is remembered, and `observe_rule` goes through `hold_scoped_rule`, guarded the same way. A
read-only benchmark run on main is safe on that count.

### COMMITTED

- **What reading forgives, saying does not produce** ((104)'s first open item; it needed no approval because reading
  does not change). Agreement was a weight alone, so saying said "We'm biased." and "My dog've bite Tom." and reading
  read them back to the very meaning they were made for. The refusal now holds only while the grammar is saying
  (`Grammar._saying`, set by `say` alone) and only on evidence against: a form memory holds few subjects of, a
  subject it holds no features of, and features no subject was ever written with refuse nothing.
- The carried preposition, its guard measurement, `whom`, and the record-cache tooling. 84 grammar tests and 126
  derived-reading tests pass.

### OPEN

1. **The end-to-end number needs main, read-only.** UNDERSTANDS-PROSE-02 has not run since main was re-taught (96)
   or since (103)'s `same_as`, so 7.8% of questions is a figure for a store that no longer exists. The sandbox holds
   no English, so nothing else can give it.
2. **Every figure in (99) to (104) was scored by `senses_aside`**, so each is worth re-reading against the measure
   that names both sides by their words: the four fixes (101) called net negative, (100)'s error budget and its
   "sense label costs 20.6 points", and the ERG comparison in (102), where the bridge's own naming was handled on
   one side only. The runs are on disk; nothing needs re-running to re-score the whole-meaning counts, since every
   run writes its misses.
3. The link figures (`links decided by own/kind/rule`) are still scored against the `senses_aside` gold so they stay
   comparable with earlier runs, which means they understate a reading that named a thing by another word for the
   same sense: with the records held they read 59.0% where the whole-meaning figure for the same run is 55.2%.
3. A carried preposition with a SUBJECT gap in a relative clause ("most of whom had no experience", "both of which
   are timed") — English, common in edited prose, and refused on purpose by this rule because a question cannot do
   it. Its own measured step.
4. `pp` and `pr`: a head declaring it takes a preposition phrase is what the gold has and this does not.
5. The five wrong answers of the 10-26 run are mostly the sense label reaching the person: "What is a test case?" →
   *"A test case is a kind of legal action."*, "Whom did Cyrus defeat?" → *"Cyrus. | Metier."*

## 2026-11-01 (104) — Saying could never name anything from files, and a reflexive was offered as a subject

**Objective.** Go at saying, the largest single bucket of unanswered prose questions (159 of 370 "not taught to
say"), and find out whether it can serve the answer path at all.

**The fallback was never missing.** `derived_reader.say` with no inventory tries `GrammarView.say` FIRST and falls
back to the taught constructions, so those 159 are not waiting on a grammar fallback: the grammar is asked and says
nothing. Five `give_up` preconditions guard `Grammar.say` and every one is about things or acts; `("fact", link)`
enters the budget only for links a PREPOSITION says, so a link said by a verb's role, a determiner or a copula is
checked nowhere until read-back.

**Error found, in my own harness, before any finding could be trusted.** `file_words` built `name_of` (a word ->
the thing it names) and never passed `written_for` (a thing -> the words that say it), so `HeldWords.words_for`
returned `[]` for every thing and saying could name NOTHING from files. My first measurement was 0 of 46 meanings,
every one failing in 0.0s with `no word for a thing it must say`. `on_store.py` already recorded the same artefact
(5 of 394, "the harness's figure and not the grammar's", 2026-10-29) and I should have read the saying harness
before writing another. Fixed by building the exact inverse of `name_of` over the treebank's words and WordNet's
lemmas, most used first, with a thing's own name as the fallback that carries main. Saying is now measurable from
files, which it never was.

**Measured, 46 real PMB dev meanings, 25s allowed each BY THE MEASUREMENT (never a cap in the grammar).**

| facts | said | median |
|---|---|---|
| 1-3  | 9 of 12 | ~1s |
| 4-8  | 8 of 20 | 25s (cut) |
| 9-13 | 0 of 14 | 25s (cut) |

The cliff is at four facts. AN ANSWER IS A ONE-FACT MEANING (`_said` builds exactly that), so saying is viable for
the answer path; it is full-sentence generation that collapses, which is a different use and not what the 159 need.

**Error found and fixed: a pronoun of its own sentence was offered as a SUBJECT.** "Myself", "ourselves",
"himself" say the thing their doing is done by, so each stands where that thing stands again and nowhere else.
`_stands_as_written` asks this of a thing standing AFTER the verb; nothing asked it of a subject. Saying said
"Myself'm oldest." and "Myself payed for the bag with a 200 dollar bill.", and READING READ THEM BACK to exactly
the meanings they were made for, so the round trip could not refuse them.

Guarding the two application routes changed nothing, because the subject is taken by a third: `>T>B`, a thing
raised to what is said of it and composed with the verb BEFORE the rest of the sentence. The derivation named it:
`>T>B  S[dcl]/(S[adj]\NP.?speaker)  [0:2]`. That rule's own comment had already recorded the same shape of defect
("Owl'm birds." read so, agreement weighed only the other way of reading it). Guarded at all three.

**Verified.** `Myself'm oldest.` -> `I'm oldest.`; 17 of 46 said, from 16; said under 5s 11, from 10. Reflexive
OBJECTS untouched: "Tom chased himself." still `done_by(?v0, tom) & done_to(?v0, tom)`, "I chased myself." still
`done_to(?v0, ?speaker)`. 248 tests pass, the derived-reading suite's 122 among them.

**Verified separately, on `lyric_dev`, through the real conversation layer** (reading bypassed with the question's
meaning, since lyric_dev holds no English): UNDERSTANDS-PROSE-02's FIRST question, "Is South Asia a sub-region of
Asia?", answered "Yes." where it had answered "I hold things about south asia that I have not been taught to say
yet." -- the recall dump, which is reached only when nothing answered. "Is South Asia southern?" answered "Yes."
with `because ['south asia -> sub region 1 -> southern']`. Both needed entry (103)'s `same_as`.

**41 of the 159 "not taught to say" are yes/no questions**, which need no vocabulary for the relation at all, only
a verdict. They were never a saying problem: the reasoner returned nothing, so the reply fell through to the recall
dump, which then could not say the facts either. Two failures stacked.

**Still open, and both are the owner's call.**
- AGREEMENT IS A WEIGHT, NOT A CONSTRAINT. `_agreed` returns `min(0.0, log(...))`, so a disagreeing form can win on
  frequency and reading accepts it back, which is why the round trip keeps "We'm biased." and "My dog've bite Tom."
  Making it a constraint changes the READER, so it needs approval and a GRAMMAR-01 run to show it costs no reading.
- SEVEN ANSWER LINKS HAVE NO ENGLISH AT ALL: `requires`, `enables`, `prevents`, `caused_by`, `required_by`,
  `synonym_of`, `defined_as` -- read from every table in `Lexicon.learned`, not a chosen few. Four are relations the
  substrate reasons with, so it can derive a causal answer and have no way to say it. That is lessons, not code.

## 2026-11-01 (103) — One word for two relations: identity was inert, and that was the whole of the zero-step failure

**Objective.** Find the first verified failure in the reasoning pathway for the South Asia question, and make the
smallest architecture-consistent correction. The owner's own reading of the problem was the one to test: *"its
language system can express relationships the reasoning algebra does not yet adequately distinguish or support."*

**The chain, traced and verified on `lyric_dev`.** Reading, minting, binding, scoping, the overlay, relation
decoding and term normalisation ALL WORK. `load_subgraph(['south_asia'], actor=...)` returned five typed edges
including `same_as(south_asia, sub_region_1)`, `part_of(sub_region_1, asia)` and `has_property(sub_region_1,
southern)`. `derive_from` returned ONE derivation: `south_asia equals south_asia`, a self-loop by transitivity.
`answer_over_graph` said `unknown` with both edges in hand.

Cause: `compose(EQUALS, r)` and `compose(r, EQUALS)` are `None` for every `r`, by design — nothing chains through
arithmetic. But the reader emitted `equals` for EVERY copula, arithmetic or not, because the meaning language had
one word for both. `pmb_meanings`' own comment recorded the conflation: `equals` served both *"The capital of France
is Paris."* and *"the sum of two and three"*.

**Two of my own earlier claims were wrong, and both cost time:**
- *"Nothing reaches the world's concept graph, so the reasoner has no edges."* True that nothing does, but it is BY
  DESIGN (`Conversation._actor`: "THERE IS NO CONVERSATION THAT TEACHES THE SUBSTRATE FACTS", tightened on purpose
  because the old substrate fallback made talking a second door into the shared mind). Conversational facts reach
  the reasoner through the SCOPED OVERLAY (`load_subgraph(actor=...)` unions `edges_for_actor`), which I had missed.
  The world graph being empty is irrelevant to this failure.
- *"Relation names do not round-trip (`'has property'` vs `has_property`)."* Wrong. `_typed_edge` decodes spaces to
  underscores explicitly, in one place, by design.

**The correction.** `SemanticRelation.SAME_AS` — one thing under two descriptions — distinct from `EQUALS` (two
values that are the same number) and from `SYNONYM_OF` (two words that mean the same, which already owns the
surface form "same as"). Symmetric, always transitive, not inheritable, not generic-safe, no surface forms: reading
decides it from the construction. `relation_algebra.compose` gained renaming in BOTH argument positions
(`one_thing_under_two_descriptions`), and `spell_out`'s copula now says `equals` only when either side is a number.
`pmb_meanings` and `erg_meanings` (`appos`, `id`) draw the same line, so the benchmark compares like with like.

Renaming carries the other relation through UNCHANGED, so it licenses nothing that relation did not already
license: `a same_as b`, `b made_of steel`, `steel isa alloy` still refuses `a isa alloy`. Arithmetic is sealed off
from renaming (`_NO_RENAMING`): a number is not a thing under two descriptions, reading never puts one in `SAME_AS`,
so sealing it costs nothing and stops a wrong identity propagating a numeric claim.

**Error found and fixed, pre-existing, shared by two call sites.** `spell_out`'s `numeric(t)` asked
`_number(str(t))`. The unknowns a reading mints are ints (`fresh()` returns negatives) and `term` spells every int
as `?x`/`?y`, so the mint's own counter read as a written number and EVERY described thing was numeric.
`_number(str(-5))` is `'-5'`. Two consequences: the new copula rule said `equals` for "Tom is the dog.", and the
comparative at the other call site read *"Rex is more careful than the dog."* as two numbers compared with no degree
of carefulness between them. Fixed at the helper, which repairs both: a written number is only ever a `str`.

**Verified.**
- `lyric_dev`, through the real overlay and the real algebra, actor-scoped: `south asia has_property southern` →
  `true` and `south asia instance_of sub-region` → `true`, both previously `unknown`, both derived via
  `one_thing_under_two_descriptions`, and NEITHER held in the shared graph (checked and printed first).
  `south asia part_of europe` → `unknown`: open-world preserved, nothing confabulated.
- 122 tests pass: grammar 81, teaching path 8, relations + algebra 33.
- New regression tests cover identity substitution both ways, arithmetic staying inert, no inheritance down a kind
  and no place-reading, an identity cycle terminating, and a derived fact naming its rule and carrying the evidence
  of every edge it went through.
- The existing `done_by`/`done_to` isolation test was amended, not weakened: renaming REPLACES an argument rather
  than chaining through the link ("done by Alice, Alice is the mayor, so done by the mayor"), and the test that no
  kind of a participant leaks into the event still guards the thing it was written for.
- PMB dev gold: 33 copula sentences, all `same_as`, none arithmetic — the gold and the reader draw the same line on
  this split, so the `_ARITHMETIC` guard is dormant there and cannot regress it.

**Not measured yet.** The effect on GRAMMAR-01 and UNDERSTANDS-PROSE-02. Both are the owner's runs to start. What
they should show: the reading score roughly unchanged (one relation renamed on both sides of the comparison), and
the reasoner taking steps where it took none on 0 of 362 factual questions.

**Still open.** 159 of 370 unanswered prose questions are "not taught to say" — the largest single bucket, and
untouched by this. `Grammar.say` works but took 58 min / 15.9 GB on one meaning, so it is not wired behind
`_said()`. The `pp`/`pr` grammar refactor (22.1% of dev words have a gold category Lyric cannot express, 52% of it
one design decision) remains unapproved. `hold_for_person` has no `remembered()` guard where the neighbouring
`hold_scoped_relation` does, so a `remembers=False` conversation may still persist scoped rows — worth checking
against main, which I cannot read.

## 2026-11-01 (102) — The English Resource Grammar reads here, and the 95% bar is outside the state of the art

**Objective.** *"ok lets do it. You don't need to come back to me until reading and responding is above the 95%
bar"* — after (101) showed four hand-traced fixes net negative, use a grammar that already exists instead of
building one.

### What already exists, and what does not

| | what it is | licence | not a model? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ERG + ACE** | hand-written HPSG grammar of English, 20+ years, 225 syntactic and 70 lexical rules | **MIT** | **yes** |
| PyDelphin | Python for it, v1.11.0, active | MIT | — |
| UDepLambda | UD to lambda forms | Apache 2.0 | yes, but stale ~9.5 years, pulls in GPL CoreNLP |
| depccg / Issen | CCG parsers, 94.0 F1 | MIT code | **no** — neural; weights from LDC CCGbank |
| Boxer | made the PMB's gold | **unclear**, unmaintained | yes |

What nobody ships, and nobody could, is **MRS to Lyric's meaning language**: one side of that table is
`done_by`/`done_to`/`instance_of`/`located_in`, which is Lyric's own. The download covers English to formal
semantics. The bridge is ours.

**Two blockers, each looking like something else.** ACE mmaps its grammar image at a hardcoded address
(`FREEZER_MMAP_BASE`); the macOS build on offer predates the Apple Silicon fix (r1096) and dies with *"mmap didn't
put the freezer where i wanted it"*. The Linux 0.9.34 build runs under Docker. And without a UTF-8 locale ACE fails
decoding a curly apostrophe **in the grammar's own data**, on sentences containing no such character.

### THE DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE INVALIDATED EVERY NUMBER

`erg_parse.read` matched ACE's output to its input **by place**. ACE writes `SENT: <the sentence>` before what it
read — **but not for every sentence given it**: of 1,194 it echoed 1,178, passing over `Where art thou?` and fifteen
others in silence. From the first silence on, every sentence was scored against another sentence's meaning: the
whole split came out at **2.9%** where its first hundred came out at **20.8%**, which is the only reason the bug
showed itself. Aligned now by the sentence ACE echoes.

### Where it lands

`20261101T014320Z` and the run after it, both against `20261028T111052Z`:

| | Lyric's grammar | ERG + the bridge |
|---|---:|---:|
| read at all | 891 of 911 | **897 of 911** |
| senses aside: whole right | **42.4%** | 17.1% |
| senses aside: facts F1 | **0.821** | 0.658 |
| + the one spoken of before unnamed | **53.6%** | 20.6% |

The ERG reads MORE sentences and its meanings are LESS accurate — the bridge is hours old against a grammar that has
had weeks. On the sentences (101) spent a day on it is exactly right where Lyric is wrong:

```
'He walked in the park.'             _in_p_loc ARG1=the walking ARG2=the park   -> located_in
'Where did Mahatma Gandhi study?'    loc_nonsp + place_n + which_q, study ARG2 unfilled
'The book is on the table.'          _on_p_loc ARG1=the book ARG2=the table
```

`Where did Mahatma Gandhi study?` and `Nobody walks in LA.` come out EXACTLY as the gold.

### AND THE MEASURE STOPS RESPONDING

Six conventions bridged, each verified on its own sentences, each read off the gold rather than guessed:
coordination of things as a group (`has_member`) and of happenings as two happenings; a quality naming a place as
`comes_from` by WordNet's pertainym; a possessive as `part_of` of a body part; the copula as no happening at all; a
pronoun by person **and** number; a time as the literal it says.

The whole-meaning score across those six: **15.0 → 20.8 → 20.8 → 17.7 → 18.0 → 16.9 → 17.1.**

**Making the code correct lowered it twice.** Fixing the ordering so the possessive rule fired at all and so a
conjunction of names joined names rather than unknowns cost 1.1 points. The gold encodes an **annotator's manual**,
and both readings of a sentence are often right English with only one in the manual: `I am Korean.` is
`comes_from(?speaker, korea)` there and `has_property(?speaker, korean)` by any ordinary reading; a body part is
sometimes `part_of` and sometimes `owned_by`; `Let us go!` is a future; "CDs" is `compact disk`. There is no
gradient to climb.

### WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE 95% BAR

Exact whole-meaning match needs very nearly every fact right. Two points measured today:

| facts F1 | whole meanings right |
|---:|---:|
| 0.821 (Lyric) | 42.4% |
| 0.658 (this bridge) | 17.1% |

**95% of whole meanings needs facts F1 of about 0.99.** The best published parsing of this corpus is **89.3 Counter
F1** (one 2024 claim of 91.5), and **Boxer — the hand-built system that MADE this gold — scores 74.3**, and is
admitted by its own authors to be partly tuned on the dev and test sets. Nobody is within reach of 0.99.

So **95% of whole meanings exactly right is not a bar this benchmark can be held to, by Lyric or by anything else
that exists.** It is not a statement about Lyric's grammar.

### What the bar should be instead, and what to do

1. **Hold the bar on a graded measure or on answering.** Facts F1 (Lyric 0.821 today) is the measure comparable to
   the published 0.89–0.91. For "reading AND RESPONDING", the honest measure is questions answered right end to end:
   UNDERSTANDS-PROSE-02 has that at **9.4% of questions**, which is where the headroom actually is and where 95%
   means something a user would feel.
2. **Keep Lyric's grammar.** On this evidence it is more than twice as accurate as ERG plus a young bridge, and the
   bridge has no gradient.
3. **Use the ERG as an ORACLE.** It found three real Lyric defects in minutes, and (101)'s category measurement
   stands: 22.1% of the gold's categories Lyric cannot express, over half of that one design decision — no `pp` and
   no `pr`, so a preposition must choose among six modifier categories at the preposition where the PMB lets the
   head declare it takes a phrase.

### Open

1. The `pp`/`pr` refactor of `english.json` (101), still the largest measured inventory gap, still unapproved.
2. The three tests asked for before calling the pipeline integrated: translation loss is now **named and counted**
   (180 gaps over 911, `nothing said for` 97, `class` 43, `predicate` 18, `quantifier` 17); reasoning integration is
   **not started** and needs a store, `lyric_dev` only; round-trip generation is **not started**, and ACE generates
   as well as parses, so there are two round-trips worth measuring and they fail differently.
3. From (101): the record's preposition links overrule taught sentences with no bookkeeping to separate them.

## 2026-10-31 (101) — The word records fix the sense label and wreck the structure: one record overruled every sentence taught about the verb. "Where" asked what a doing was done to; a quality could mean no sense but its most frequent

**Objective.** *"continue.... you mentioned 3 things and none of them need my decision"* — the three things (100)
left waiting: run GRAMMAR-01 with the word records, fix the preposition's link, and give a quality and an adverb a
sense at all.

### The preposition's link: the real population is not the sentence I named

(100) closed on *"`He walked in the park.` reads `has_property(?v0, ?v1)` where `located_in` belongs; `located_in` is
missed 11 times over the split"*. Read off the run's own record of what it missed
(`20261028T111656Z_missed.json`), that is **21** sentences whose meaning says `located_in` and whose reading does
not (8 the other way round), and they are not one defect:

| shape | n | |
|---|---|---|
| a question whose "where" is not read as asking a place | **8** | `Where did Mahatma Gandhi study?`, `Where did Golda Meir grow up?`, `Where did you guys meet?`, `But where is this compass?`, `Where art thou?`, `In which city is he?`, `What country is Berlin in?`, `What band was Jerry Garcia with?` |
| the preposition's own link learned wrong | 3 | `Nobody walks in LA.` → `has_property(?v0, la)`; `Is English spoken in Canada?` → `about(english, canada)` |
| a word memory knows several words as beats the literal reading | 1 | `She doesn't speak Japanese at home.` — "at home" read as the THING that speaks |
| a verb's frames | 1 | `He collided with a tree.` → `done_by` twice |
| a quality's link | 1 | `Dagbladet is a Norwegian newspaper.` → `comes_from` |
| the rest | 7 | |

So the sentence I named is 1 of 21, and the dominant shape is the question word. **Fix what the measurement says, not
what the example says.**

### "Where" spent the adverb's uses, so a cheaper parse decided what it meant

The grammar reads "where" four ways. Three make a `prep` piece saying it asks a place; one
(`where:object`) says it is the thing a doing is done to, and **that one declared `"use": "wh:adverb"`** — the
adverb's use. Every entry of a grammar word is weighed by how often a treebank uses the word that way
(`Lexicon.entries`: `evidence.get(e["use"], -20.0)`), so the two readings weighed **exactly the same**, and what the
rest of the sentence cost decided which. A doing with its object filled is cheaper than one with an adjunct, so
`Where did Mahatma Gandhi study?` asked WHAT Gandhi studied.

The treebank already signs the two apart (`grammar_words.HeldWords._use`: `wh:adverb` where the word modifies the
doing, `wh:object` where it is the object), and it is decisive:

| word | `wh:adverb` | `wh:object` |
|---|---|---|
| where | 16 | **0** |
| what | — | 76 |
| who | — | 4 |
| which | — | 3 |

"Where" is never a doing's object in UD English EWT's training part, which is right for English. One word changed in
`data/grammar/english.json`; the entry **remains**, so a sentence no other reading composes for is still read by it
(`Where did the dog chase?` still asks what was chased, "chase" being only ever said with a thing).

**Verified** by reverting the one word and reading the same 15 sentences with words held from files: 2 read "where"
as asking a place before, **5** after; `Where did you guys meet?`, `Where did Mahatma Gandhi study?` and `Where is
the station?` gained, and the full diff of both readings touches no other sentence — "who", "what", "when" and "how"
are untouched. The regression test (`test_where_asks_a_place_and_never_what_a_doing_was_done_to`) was proved to
discriminate: with the word reverted, `Where did the dog study?` asks what was studied.

**A defect found while writing that test.** The test first asserted on `Where did the dog sleep?` and passed either
way: the fixture had no verb said both transitively and intransitively, so no competition could arise and the test
measured nothing. "study" was added to the fixture with both frames. A test that passes before the fix is not a test.

### A quality and an adverb had no sense mechanism at all

`thing_sense_of` takes a noun's sense and `sense_of` a verb's. **Nothing took a quality's or an adverb's.**
`hold_word` loaded sense tables for nouns and verbs alone, `spell_out` asked nothing, and the quality branch said
`words.name(word, "ADJECTIVE")` — which is WordNet's name for the sense the word names most often. And the data was
not there either: `_semcor_seen` read verbs alone (`t.synset().pos() == "v"`), so no word record carried anything of
a quality's senses.

Built in the three places the noun's and the verb's are built: `_semcor_seen` records what a quality and an adverb
were **said of** (a quality of a thing, an adverb of a doing — the word the structure joins it to, and the subject
where a copula says it of one); `Lexicon.quality_used` and `quality_seen`, held under the name **and** the kind of
word, since a word said both ways is named the same for both ("fast"); and `Lexicon.quality_sense_of`, asked in the
quality branch and the adverb branch by what the sentence means of the thing or doing it is said of, so the thing's
own sense is taken first and the quality's by it.

**The research decided the form.** `WORD_SENSES.md` §7.4 (SENSE-SAID-01, 12,654 of WordNet's hand-tagged pairs):

| | verb–object | adjective–noun |
|---|---|---|
| most frequent sense | 56.6% | 57.4% |
| what it is said of first, frequency on a tie | 44.6% | **42.5%** |
| the two added as one number in nats | 58.3% | **58.8%** |

So how often a sense is used is **added**, never ranked under — `ln(used/total)` plus `ln(P(k|c)/P(k))` over each
kind the thing is, averaged, one use spread as anything is. That is the same form `thing_sense_of` and `sense_of`
already take, which I checked before writing a line: both start from the frequency prior in nats and add the
strength. A quality said of a thing nothing was ever seen said of keeps its most frequent sense.

WordNet gives an adjective no kinds, so neither the information a shared kind carries nor a verb's places can be
asked of one. What it was seen said of is all there is.

**Verified.** `_semcor_seen` was held to what it makes of a sentence, not to what a corpus happens to hold: the
cache is seeded with real WordNet lemmas and structure reads written out, so the test reads no SemCor and no
treebank (3.8s). A quality `amod` of a noun and a quality said of a noun by a copula both record
`("said_of", curry.n.01)`; an adverb records its doing; the verb's own subject and object are untouched. End to end,
`The curry is hot.` reads `has_property(?v0, spicy hot)` where it read `hot`, and `The dog is hot.` and `A hot dog
barked.` do not move — proved to come from asking the sense by answering `quality_sense_of` with the bare name and
re-reading. 86 tests pass (`test_grammar.py` 78, `test_teaching_path.py` 8).

**Expected size: small.** The research prices fine-grained adjective–noun choice at 1.4 points over most-frequent
sense. This closes a hole in what reading *can* do; it is not a large share of its gap.

### THE RUN: the word records fix the sense label and wreck the structure

`20261031T211729Z`, GRAMMAR-01 with `--with-words` — 6,986 words recorded whole, 2,848s. It crashed first on my own
block from (100): `TaughtSentence.text`, which does not exist; the field is `sentence`. It loaded the grammar and the
teaching sources before the two fixes above, so it prices the word-record layer **alone** against
`20261028T111052Z`, which is the same experiment with the records switched off:

| | no records | with records | |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| strict: whole meaning right | 21.84% | **25.14%** | **+3.3** |
| strict: facts F1 | 0.468 | **0.513** | **+4.5** |
| senses aside: whole meaning right | **42.37%** | 31.83% | **−10.5** |
| senses aside: facts F1 | **0.821** | 0.637 | **−18.4** |
| + the one spoken of before unnamed | **53.57%** | 40.61% | −13.0 |
| links by the word's own uses, right | **1,172 of 1,443 (81.2%)** | 872 of 1,437 (60.7%) | **−20.5** |
| links by what it is a kind of | 93 of 173 (53.8%) | 44 of 96 (45.8%) | −8.0 |
| links by the grammar's rule | 69 of 169 (40.8%) | 35 of 101 (34.7%) | −6.1 |
| read, meaning wrong | 498 | 591 | +93 |

(100) predicted the records would be *"the lever on both gaps at once"*. **Half right, and the half that is wrong is
larger.** They do what was predicted for the sense label. They also decide 300 more of the same number of links
WRONG. The senses-aside drop is not a measurement artefact: `senses_aside` renames the **gold** by the reading's own
word names (`names_of`, from the winning sign's `word` pieces), so the sense label is neutralised there by
construction and a drop can only be structure.

**THE CAUSE, traced and shown with no run at all.** `GrammarView.learn` counts what a taught meaning said of each
place of a verb into `learned["role"][(name, slot)]`; `hold_word` counts the word record's PropBank places into **the
same counter**. `_weighed` takes the most said, and PropBank's count is the larger, so **one word record overruled
every sentence ever taught about that verb.** Filling the two counters by hand, exactly as the two callers fill them:

```
after one taught sentence ("You tortured a prisoner."):
    learned['role'][('torture','subject')] = {'done_by': 1}        inherited -> ('done_by', 'own')
after the word record is held on top:
    learned['role'][('torture','subject')] = {'done_by': 1, 'has_property': 5}
    place_links[('torture','subject')]     = {'has_property': 5}   inherited -> ('has_property', 'own')
```

VerbNet's only class of "torture" is one of feelings (`amuse-31.1`: "NP:Stimulus V NP:Experiencer"), so the record
turned the torturer into what causes a feeling — and this is the verb whose docstring already records the same defect
being found from the other direction in lyric_dev2 on 2026-10-29.

**The bookkeeping to fix it was already there and unused.** `hold_word` records PropBank's own share apart
(`place_links`) for exactly this purpose, and `taught_role` already states the rule — *"what was said of the very verb
is not overruled by its frames"* — but **only `framed` consulted it.** The place decision now does the same
(`_taught_apart`): PropBank's share comes out of the counter and what taught sentences said decides where they said
anything. A verb nobody taught still takes its PropBank places, which beat the grammar's own link alone. No other
table is touched, and the regression test was proved to discriminate.

**Same shape, not fixed, no bookkeeping to separate the two:** `hold_word` also counts the record's preposition links
into `learned["prep"]`, `learned["prep_to"]` and `learned["prep_of"]`, which taught sentences also fill, and there is
no `place_links` for them. `prep_of` wins outright in the preposition branch (`if how_own == "own"`), so a record's
preposition link overrides every taught sentence about that verb's preposition.

### THE FOUR FIXES MEASURED: net negative, and MY CLAIMED CAUSE IS WRONG

`20261031T220938Z`, the same 6,986 records with all four of today's fixes ("where", the quality's sense, the
adverb's sense, and `_taught_apart`):

| | records only | + the four fixes | |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| strict: whole meaning right | 25.14% (229) | 25.25% (230) | +1 sentence |
| strict: facts F1 | 0.513 | 0.517 | +0.4 |
| senses aside: whole meaning right | 31.83% (290) | **29.97% (273)** | **−17 sentences** |
| senses aside: facts F1 | 0.637 | **0.623** | **−1.4** |
| + the one spoken of before unnamed | 40.61% (370) | **38.20% (348)** | **−22** |
| links by the word's own uses, right | 872 of 1,437 (60.7%) | **848 of 1,438 (59.0%)** | **−24 right** |
| links by what it is a kind of | 44 of 96 (45.8%) | 41 of 96 (42.7%) | −3 |
| links by the grammar's rule | 35 of 101 (34.7%) | 29 of 101 (28.7%) | −6 |

**ERROR, CORRECTED HERE.** Commit `270ad380` and the paragraph above state that PropBank's places overruling the
taught counter **is the cause** of the records' 20-point structural regression. **It is not.** Taking the overruling
out recovered nothing: links decided by a word's own uses went 60.7% → 59.0%, slightly *worse*. The overruling is
real — it is shown by construction, by filling the two counters exactly as their two callers fill them — but it is
not what costs the points. I verified that the mechanism exists and then asserted it was the cause without measuring
that, which is the same mistake (99) made and (100) corrected.

So the records' structural damage comes from something else `hold_word` writes: the forms, the uses each word is put
to, `verb_frames`, the name a word is read under (`recorded_name` — which changes what every kind in every reading is
called), the knowledge `isa` links, or `learned["prep"]`/`prep_to`/`prep_of`. Not yet separated.

**And the four fixes cannot be separated from each other** by this run: each was verified on its own sentences with a
test proved to discriminate, and together they are net −1.9 points of whole meanings with senses aside. Separating
them is four more runs. Each costs 62 minutes, of which **3,674 of 3,707 seconds is recording the 6,986 words** — the
reading itself is 33 seconds. Caching the records to disk would make a variant run about a minute, and separating
four fixes four minutes instead of four hours. That is the measurement tool this loop has been missing all day.

**What the day's arithmetic says.** Four fixes, each traced to a named cause in the code, each with a discriminating
regression test, each measured right on the sentences it was about: **net worse on the held-out split.** Taken with
the fact that this task has a published rule-based reference implementation (Boxer, 74.3, the tool that made the
PMB's own gold) and that GRAMMAR-01's facts F1 is its own measure and not the Counter the published numbers use, the
honest reading is that the defect-at-a-time loop is not converging and the next move is a measurement one, not
another fix.

### Found, not fixed: a word memory knows several words as always beats the literal reading

`The book is on the table.` reads `has_property(?v0, "on the table")` — WordNet holds "on the table" as an adjective
(the idiom), and nothing of the table survives in the meaning. `Tom is at home.` reads `equals(tom, ?v0) &
instance_of(?v0, "at home")` — WordNet's "at home" is a reception. `She doesn't speak Japanese at home.` is the same
defect in the dev split.

The cause is in four lines of `Lexicon._together`: a word memory knows several words as is scored
`sum(max(evidence per word))` — **every one of its words at its most likely use**, which is the ceiling for that
span. So it ties or beats every reading built from those same words, however rare the idiom. And the score does not
depend on the class, so "at home" as a thing and "at home" as an adverb weigh exactly the same though a word's kinds
are never equally likely. `uses("on the table")` is 0.0: EWT tokenises them apart, so there is no count to weigh the
whole by, and the honest scale would have to come from the treebank's own `fixed`/`flat` joins. **Not touched** —
re-weighing every multiword entry changes reading broadly, and that is a change to ask for, not to make.

### Found, measured, NOT fixed: a fronted preposition phrase is read as an adverb named by the bare word

`In which city is he?` reads `has_property(?v1, in)` — "in" becomes an adverb named `in`, said of a variable nothing
else in the meaning mentions, and "which city" becomes a thing linked to nobody. `On the table is a book.` reads
`has_property(?v2, on)` **and equates the table with the book**. `In Boston he lives.` reads correctly
(`word_in(?v0, boston)`), so the failure is specifically a fronted phrase before an inverted copula.

**Sized before touching it:** of the 525 dev misses, **2** read a preposition as a quality named by the bare word,
and both are particles ("clean up", "out of fashion"), not fronted phrases. `In which city is he?` is 1 sentence in
911. Left alone: the shape the PMB's dev split does not contain is not what reading's gap is made of, and the
measurement said so before an hour went into it.

### Open

1. **The 375 truly apart (41.2%)**, unchanged from (100): a doing's Co-Agent place (24), which link a possessive
   says (13), a doing of three places (13), a word standing where a thing belongs (26 sentences, 37 links).
2. **The two runs' numbers**, and GRAMMAR-01's README and RunRecord from them.
3. **A word of several words outscoring its own words**, above; and a fronted preposition phrase, above (1 sentence
   in 911, so last).
4. `Where art thou?` reads no whole; `But where is this compass?` hangs the place on the wrong thing; `In which city
   is he?` does not read a fronted preposition phrase.
5. The verb side of sense choice: `Tom plays the piano.` still reads `play` for `sound play`.
6. From (100): saying's 22 silent and 30 wrong; no universal quantifier, no noun number, no degree in the meaning
   language.

## 2026-10-31 (100) — Reading's gap, taken apart: the sense label costs 20.6 points, the naming convention 13.6, and 41% is truly wrong

**Objective.** *"ok perfect so lets fix"* — fix reading, after (99) named word senses its binding defect.

**ERROR IN (99), CORRECTED HERE.** (99) says the 279 reading failures *"are ONE defect with 205 instances"* and that
*"reading has no word sense disambiguation; it takes the most frequent sense and context never enters."* Both are
wrong, and the code says so:

- `Lexicon.thing_sense_of` (nouns, Resnik 1995 over the other things a sentence names) and `Lexicon.sense_of` (verbs,
  Resnik 1993 over what fills each place, from SemCor's tagged uses) are both built, both called from `spell_out`,
  and both read tables main holds for 2,667 nouns and 1,430 verbs. Context DOES enter.
- The 279 are not one defect. They are four blocks of very different size and very different cost, and the
  measurement that separates them was already on disk.

**WHAT READING'S GAP IS MADE OF**, from GRAMMAR-01's own run `20261028T111052Z` (the PMB's held-out dev split, 911
sentences) and from that run's record of every sentence it missed (`20261028T111656Z_missed.json`, 525 of them, with
senses already set aside on both sides). No run was started for this; the numbers below are that run's, re-read:

| | right whole | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| strict — each fine-grained WordNet sense counted | 199 | 21.8% | facts F1 0.468 |
| senses set aside — both sides named by the word | 386 | 42.4% | facts F1 0.821 |
| + which unknown is which (reading says `?previous` where the PMB leaves an unknown) | 510 | 56.0% | |
| + a word put where the PMB puts a thing of that kind | 536 | 58.8% | |
| **truly apart — a word or a link genuinely wrong** | **375** | **41.2%** | |

So the sense LABEL costs 20.6 points of whole meanings and 35 points of fact F1; which unknown is which costs 13.6
more (GRAMMAR-01 already measures that third way: 53.6%); a word used where a thing belongs 2.8; and 41% is
genuinely wrong. **Reading's structure is right in 58.8% of held-out sentences and its facts at F1 0.821 with the
sense label set aside.** The grammar is not the binding defect; (99) had that part right for the wrong reason.

**AND THE SENSE MACHINERY WAS NEVER MEASURED.** GRAMMAR-01 never calls `GrammarView.hold_word`, so `thing_used`,
`thing_covers`, `sense_used` and `sense_seen` are all empty in it. Its strict 21.8% is the most frequent sense of
every word, with no sense choice running at all. The experiment that measures reading does not exercise the one
mechanism that would move its strict number.

**OF THE 291 MISSES THAT NAME EVERY WORD RIGHT**, what differs:

| | meanings | |
|---|---|---|
| only which unknown is which | 124 | `He ate the apple.`: `done_by(?v0, ?previous)` for `done_by(?v0, ?v1)` |
| the meaning's `done_by`, reading's `done_to` | 15 | `Tom embraces Marie.`, `Castro visits the UN.`: a doing whose second place VerbNet gives a Co-Agent |
| the meaning's `done_to`, reading's `done_by` | 9 | |
| the meaning's `part_of` / `creates`, reading's `owned_by` | 13 | `He was ashamed of his ignorance.`: which link a possessive says |
| the meaning's `received_by`, reading's `done_to` | 4 (+9 put in) | a doing of three places |
| `instance_of` missed, a word standing where a thing belongs | 37 links | `We buy CDs.`: `done_to(?v0, cds)` for `done_to(?v0, ?v2) & instance_of(?v2, cds)` |

**WHAT THE RESEARCH ALREADY SAYS ABOUT THE SENSE LABEL** (`docs/research/WORD_SENSES.md`, 2026-10-01, measured on
12,654 of WordNet's hand-tagged pairs, SENSE-SAID-01): the most frequent sense is 56.6% on verb–object and 57.4% on
adjective–noun; what a word is said of, added, gives 58.3% and 58.8%; taken FIRST it falls to 44.6% and 42.5%. The
knowledge-based random walk over WordNet (Agirre et al. 2014) is 59.7 against 60.1 for the most frequent sense
fine-grained, and 80.1 coarse. **Fine-grained sense choice has about one to two points of headroom over the most
frequent sense and forty at the coarse level.** So the 20.6 points the label costs are not 20.6 points of
understanding: most of the pairs are one coarse sense (`product book` for `book`, `foodstuff egg` for `egg`,
`building school` for `school`, `tract park` for `park`, `food water` for `water`). The 41% truly apart is where
understanding is actually lost.

**BUILT.**

1. **A thing of several words was read under a name no thing has.** What memory knows two words as together is held
   in one place, `Words.known_words`. `Words.known_name` and `Words.known_verb` answered `None` of their own instead
   of asking it, so any `Words` holding only `known_words` — the one the contract names — said memory knows nothing
   of several words. A noun before a noun then named the thing by its own words: `Did you bring a hair dryer?` was
   `hair dryer`, a name no thing has, so nothing memory holds of the thing reached the reading, and the two words
   were read under two names at once, this one and `known_words`' `hand blower`, weighed on two scales. Both now name
   the thing memory holds. `df3d3d6a`.

2. **A thing's sense is taken by the place of the doing it fills.** `thing_sense_of` was given only the other THINGS
   a sentence names, and `He ate the egg.` names two things of which neither is a kind of the other, so nothing was
   offered and the most frequent sense was taken whatever the doing said. `sense_seen` already holds what each sense
   of each doing was seen done to and by (SemCor's tagged uses, loaded for 1,052 verbs on main); it was read in one
   direction only — the thing choosing the doing's sense, never the doing choosing the thing's. Resnik (1997), whom
   `sense_of` already cites, takes both by the one preference. `spell_out` now remembers which place of which doing
   each thing fills, with the sense the sentence means of the doing, and `thing_sense_of` weighs each candidate sense
   by how often that sense of the doing was seen with a thing that IS one.

**MEASURED, on eight sentences with the words recorded whole** (`word_record_of`, WordNet and SemCor as they are
taught; words from files as GRAMMAR-01 holds them, no store, nothing written):

| | what it reads now | |
|---|---|---|
| `He ate the egg.` | **`foodstuff egg`** | was `egg`; eating was seen done to food |
| `Tom wrote a letter.` | `letter` | right before and after |
| `The dog chased a cat.` | `cat` | right before and after |
| `Tom is reading a book.` | `book` for `product book` | both senses are a kind of product; coarse-same |
| `We drank the water.` | `water` for `food water` | both are a kind of substance; coarse-same |
| `Tom plays the piano.` | `play` for `sound play` | the DOING's sense, which `sense_of` takes and this did not touch |
| `She went to school.` | `school` for `building school` | the place is `moves_to`, and `sense_seen` holds subject and object alone (`_semcor_seen`) |
| `He walked in the park.` | `park` for `tract park`, and `has_property(?v0, ?v1)` for `located_in` | the preposition's link is wrong here, which is its own defect (`located_in` is missed 11 times over the split) |

So it moves what SemCor's uses can discriminate and nothing else: one of the five it could have moved, with no
sentence made worse. The two left are the same coarse sense as what reading gives, which is what the research
predicted.

**Verified.** `tests/test_grammar.py` 75 pass (four new: every way two nouns are read as one thing names the thing
memory holds; what a verb memory holds no form of says of its subject is answered once; a thing's sense is taken by
the place of the doing it fills). Nothing was taught and no store was written.

**ONE DEFECT FOUND WHILE CHECKING, FIXED.** Reading never returned. What a verb memory holds no form of says of its
subject is worked out from the verbs written as it is (`_written_like`), and that table was built by asking
`_agrees_as` of every verb that took a subject; a verb in that list memory holds no form of sent the question
straight back into the table being built, which was still empty, so it was built again from inside itself and never
stopped. `Tom is reading a book.` raised RecursionError with the words held from files. The table is now built from
the forms memory DOES hold (`_held_agreement`, lifted out of `_agrees_as`): a word memory holds nothing of says
nothing about what an ending says, and that is the answer, not a question to ask again. It can be reached on main
too -- any word memory holds no form of, read where a verb belongs.

**OPEN, in the order the measurement puts them.**

1. **The 375 truly apart (41.2%).** Named above: a doing's Co-Agent place (24), which link a possessive says (13), a
   doing of three places (13), a word standing where a thing belongs (26 sentences, 37 links). Each is a link
   decision learned from taught meanings (`learned["role"]`, `place_links`, `framed`, `inherited`), not a rule in
   code.
2. **GRAMMAR-01 holds no word records**, so its strict number never exercises sense choice. Holding them is a run.
3. **A quality and an adverb can never mean any sense but the most frequent.** `hold_word` loads sense tables for
   nouns and verbs only, and `spell_out` asks for neither for a quality: `We added something new.` can only be `new`,
   never `original fresh`. The data a quality's sense would be chosen by — what each sense was seen said of — is not
   on the record either (`_semcor_seen` reads verbs alone), so this one needs a teaching source change and a run.
4. **Multiword verbs on main.** `run into` for `meet`, `suck up to` for `cozy up`. Whether main holds WordNet's 2,770
   multi-word verbs is unchecked (`lyric_wordnet_one_class_per_word` says lyric_dev was taught them and main was not);
   `known_verb` now asks `known_words` for them wherever they are held.

## 2026-10-31 (99) — Reading picks the most frequent sense of every word, and that is the system's binding defect

**Objective.** *"FIX ALL OF THESE"*, of (98)'s open list, and then *"how far is lyric away from being able to have a
conversation"*. Twelve saying defects are fixed below, but the finding that outranks all of them is what the 279
reading failures turn out to be: nobody had ever looked at them, and they are ONE defect with 205 instances.

**WHY READING GIVES THE WRONG MEANING, over the 279 of 400 it gets wrong.** Compared only on what does not depend
on what an unknown was called -- the CONCEPTS a meaning names and the LINKS it holds:

| | meanings | |
|---|---|---|
| the same links, different words | 103 | the structure is right, the sense is wrong |
| different words and different links | 102 | |
| the same words and the same links, joined differently | 43 | both right, the attachment wrong |
| the same words, different links | 31 | |
| read nothing at all | 13 | 8 no whole reading, 3 no whole, 2 named |

**READING GETS THE STRUCTURE RIGHT IN 146 OF 279, AND 205 OF 279 TURN ON THE WRONG SENSE OF A WORD.** The wrong
senses are not near misses, they are the FIRST sense of the word every time, checked against WordNet itself:

| the meaning holds | reading gives |
|---|---|
| `product book` = `book.n.02` | `book` = `book.n.01` |
| `foodstuff egg` = `egg.n.02` | `egg` = `egg.n.01` |
| `sound play` = `play.v.07` | `play` = `play.v.01` |
| `cozy up` = `cozy_up.v.01` ("sucks up to") | `suck` = `suck.v.01` |
| `give birth` = `give_birth.v.01` ("was born") | `bear` = `bear.v.01` |
| `meet` = `meet.v.01` ("ran into") | `run` = `run.v.01` |
| `national capital` | `york` |

**Reading has no word sense disambiguation. It takes the most frequent sense and the context never enters.** Two
sub-causes, both well defined: the most-frequent-sense baseline, and a phrasal verb read as its bare verb ("ran
into", "sucks up to", "was born"). BOTH ARE FIXABLE FROM DATA THE STORE ALREADY HOLDS -- SemCor records what each
sense was seen used with (`uses` on every word record) and `together`/`joins_things` carry the multi-word units.
No new source is needed. **This is the gate on everything: reading's grammar is in far better shape than 27%
suggests, and saying cannot be judged above a ceiling reading sets.**

**TWELVE SAYING DEFECTS, AND THEY WERE ONE CAUSE.** `_piece_says` is the authority on what a grammar word says of a
meaning and it knew **11 of the 32** kinds of piece the grammar's words carry. An unknown kind counts nothing,
`_says_of` reads a nothing as *this whole entry says nothing this meaning holds*, and discards the ENTIRE ENTRY --
so one unknown kind takes every word carrying it out of English, with no error raised anywhere:

- `poss` unknown -> `my`, `your`, `his`, `her`, `their`, `mine`, `'s` offered for **no meaning at all**. No possessive.
- `now` unknown -> the entries of `is`/`am`/`are`/`'s` that make a doing going on now discarded. **No present
  progressive**, so `Tom is writing a letter.` could never be said however long saying searched.
- `asked` unknown -> every question word discarded. **No questions whatever.**
- `polite` unknown -> every modal carries it beside its own `can`, so every modal was refused by it.

Answered for now: `poss` (with the possessive bound to the thing it owns, Kay 1996, and an owner the word leaves
open bound to the owner the fact gives), `now` and `future` (the two times beside `past`, which `say` itself
already mapped the same way), `asked`, `degree_asked`, `can`, `may`, `kind`, `deny_arg`, the comparatives, `count`,
`during`. `polite`, `npi`, `gap`, `event` and `role` say nothing of a meaning's FACTS and so disqualify no word.
`prep` and `every` stay unanswered knowingly and for stated reasons.

**Seven more, each its own cause.** A noun phrase is no longer a whole telling of a meaning that asserts something,
so `a letter written by Tom` is not a finished sentence and the 274 candidates it stood for are never offered. One
thing gets one place whatever its facts call it (an `isa` subject had a NOUN place AND a NAME place, which is why
`Verga're a famous author Verga.` said the name twice). A thing memory knows as a name is said as a name, not as a
noun with a determiner (`A verga's a famous writer.`). A quality held to a degree or of a thing is said by an
adjective, not asked for as a noun (`I'm slightly hungry.`, `The show was exciting.`). A question's subject is
weighed for agreement, which NEITHER `_raised_subject` NOR `_takes_object` did -- the latter excludes it on purpose
and nothing picked it up (`How does you spell your surname?`). A multi-word form is sounded by its first word, so
"apple tree" has a first sound and `an apple tree` can be chosen -- the data was never missing, `said_before` holds
`an` before AE 89 times against `a`'s 3. And how surely a sentence was MADE ranks it, as `SAID_AT_MOST` always said
it should, instead of how probable its parse is.

**MEASURED over the 108 gold sentences main reads to exactly their annotated meaning:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| produced a correct rendering | 32 | **56** |
| said it exactly and first | 11 | 17 |
| the same words but for a contraction | — | 14 |
| differing only in a determiner or a noun's number | — | 4 |
| said it exactly, ranked below something else | 20 | 21 |
| nothing said at all | 35 | **22** |

**FOUR ERRORS OF MINE THIS SESSION, all of measurement and all corrected.**
1. **Word-for-word identity is the wrong measure of saying**, and it is the one used through (97) and (98). It
   counts `I'm intelligent.` as a failure against `I am intelligent.`: 14 of the 48 "said otherwise" are the same
   words but for a contraction.
2. **The 11/57/26/7/1 baseline of (97) was cells of a joint table**, not marginals. Corrected in (97) in place.
3. **`isa` and `has_count` were never missing links** -- the copula's `be` piece says `isa`, a numeral's place says
   `has_count`; the census matched only `("fact", link)` keys.
4. **Two reading breakdowns reported variable renaming as a defect.** Two different meanings cannot have their
   unknowns aligned by naming each one minimally: each naming is least for its OWN facts, so `?v0 read as ?v1` is
   an artifact. Only the concepts and the links are free of it, and that is what (99)'s table measures.

**WHAT A MEANING CANNOT HOLD, which caps every such measurement** (`docs/TEACHING.md` 12h): a universal quantifier
(*An owl is a bird.* and *All owls are birds.* are both `isa(owl, bird)`), a noun's number (`instance_of(?v3,
poem)` for "I write poems."), and a degree (the PMB's own annotation of "An older man was sitting on the bench." is
`has_property(?v1, aged)`). Saying answers faithfully where the meaning does not pin the words down and the
comparison calls it wrong.

**THE STANDARDISATION, MADE EXECUTABLE** (`docs/TEACHING.md` 12g). Every defect above is one side of the format
using what the other ignores: `linking` states `possessive -> owned_by` and only reading used it; `english.json`
carries 32 piece kinds and `_piece_says` knew 11. `grammar.py` now holds `SAYS_OF_A_MEANING`,
`SAYS_NOTHING_OF_A_MEANING`, `SAYS_NOTHING_OF_FACTS` and `NOT_YET_SAID`, covering exactly those 32, and
`test_every_kind_of_piece_a_grammar_word_carries_is_answered_for_in_saying` fails if the grammar's words gain a
kind saying has not answered for OR if the lists claim one the data has not got.

**Verified against the real system.** `./venv_lyric/bin/python3`, main read only, `tests/test_grammar.py` **72
passed**, two new. Nothing written to any store.

**Open, in the order the measurements put them.**
1. **Word sense disambiguation in reading.** 205 of 279. The most frequent sense is taken and context never
   enters; SemCor's `uses` is already on every word record.
2. **Phrasal verbs as units** ("ran into", "sucks up to", "was born"): `together` and `joins_things` already hold them.
3. The 43 that hold every word and every link and only join them differently -- attachment, measured but untraced.
4. Saying's 22 that say nothing and 30 that say something wrong, now a short list rather than a class.
5. The meaning language's three gaps (12h), each a change to what a meaning can HOLD.
6. (98)'s remainder: `mine` standing alone, `your` in a question, gender both halves.

## 2026-10-31 (98) — Saying could not say a possessive at all, and one unknown piece kind was why

**Objective.** *"ok lets do it. and you said links must be fixed. so here we are again fixing reading and sentence
structure AGAIN."* (97) named five links no word is offered to say and put the possessive first. His objection is
right about the process -- fixing one link at a time is the drip (95) forbade -- so the route from a link to a word
was taken whole instead, and it has ONE break in it.

**SAYING HAD ONE ROUTE FROM A LINK TO A WORD AND IT WAS PREPOSITIONS ONLY.** `Lexicon.saying(link)` reads the
`prep`, `prep_to` and `prep_of` tables and nothing else, and the loop that budgets a link
(`grammar.py`, `for link in sorted({f.relation for f in meaning.facts})`) keeps an entry only
`if entry.cls == "PREPOSITION"`. Every link that works is prepositional: `located_in`, `moves_to`, `owns`,
`word_of`, `about`, `done_for`, `moves_from`, `equals`, `done_with`, `moves_through`, `lasts_for`.

**THE BREAK IS ONE UNKNOWN PIECE KIND.** `_piece_says` enumerates the kinds saying understands -- `given`, `past`,
`be`, `deny`, `fact`, `pron` -- and its docstring says "none for any other piece". **`poss` was not among them**, so
a possessive's piece said nothing, and `_says_of` turns a nothing into `None` for the WHOLE entry. So `my`, `your`,
`his`, `her`, `their`, `mine` and `'s` were offered **for no meaning whatever**: saying has never been able to say a
possessive, while reading has read them all along from the same piece (`spell_out`'s `poss`) through the same table
(`data/grammar/english.json`'s `linking`: `"possessive": "owned_by"`). One table, used by one side.

**FIXED, both halves.** A `poss` piece says as many facts as the meaning holds of `owned_by`; and it is bound to the
thing it owns (Kay 1996 binding), only to a fact of the named owner where the word names one ("my" the speaker,
"your" the listener), the owner left open where the word leaves it open ("her", "'s"). 71 grammar tests pass, one
new: `test_a_possessive_says_what_a_thing_is_owned_by`.

**MEASURED over the 108 gold sentences main reads to exactly their annotated meaning:**

| | word for word | said otherwise | stuck, 0 read back | nothing | gave up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 11 | 61 | **28** | 7 | 1 |
| a possessive can be said | 11 | 63 | **26** | 7 | 1 |

`I lost my sunglasses.` went from **stuck at 10,000 chart items with 0 read back** to **2.0 s, 1,413 items, 8 read
back**, and `I planted an apple tree in my garden.` from stuck to **1.0 s, 438 items**. Nothing regressed. The two
that moved are the two whose possessive names its own owner (`my`); the four left are `her` and `his` (the owner
open, left to the pronoun machinery), `your` in a question, and `mine` standing alone as `NP.x`, where the owned
thing has no kind and so never becomes a place at all.

**WORD FOR WORD DID NOT MOVE, AND THE REASON IS RANKING, NOT SAYING.** `I lost my sunglasses.` is said exactly --
it is **third** in the list, behind `I've lost my sunglasses.` and `I've been losing my sunglasses.`. The tally
counts `said[0]` alone, so a right sentence ranked third counts as a failure. **Ranking is now what stands between a
working possessive and a visible gain**, and it is the next thing to measure.

**TWO ERRORS OF MINE, both corrected in (97) in place.**
- **(97)'s baseline was wrong.** I quoted 11/57/26/7/1 for the order as it stands; those were CELLS of the two-order
  joint table (where both orders agreed), not the marginals. The marginals are 11/61/28/7/1. So the charged estimate
  of (97) was **identical** to the order as it stands, not worse: the claim that it "cost two" was arithmetic of
  mine, not a measurement. Its conclusion stands -- it is not the fix.
- **(97) over-counted the missing links.** `isa` is NOT missing: `_piece_says`'s `be` kind covers `isa`, `equals`
  and `instance_of` of a name, and the census only matched `("fact", link)` keys so it missed `("be",)`. So
  `Verga're a famous author Verga.` is not a missing link; its cause is `_things_said` turning `isa(verga, writer)`
  into TWO NOUN places with nothing obliging a copula between them, which is open.

**Verified against the real system.** `./venv_lyric/bin/python3`, main read only, `tests/test_grammar.py` 71 passed.
Nothing written to any store.

**Open, in order.**
1. Ranking: the right sentence is made and ranked third. Measure how often, over the 108, the gold sentence is in
   what saying returns but not first -- that is the cheapest gain now in sight.
2. The remaining possessives: `her`/`his` with the owner open, `mine` standing alone, `your` in a question.
3. `_things_said` makes two NOUN places of one `isa` fact, and nothing obliges a copula between them.
4. The fact-coverage mask of (97), still the root fix for the 26 stuck and the 63 said otherwise; sound once every
   fact can be said, and `has_degree` and `state_of` need the corrected census before it is built.
5. Reading accepts bad English (`Me writes poems.` reads back as `I write poems.`): case and agreement read loosely.
