## 2026-10-29 (86) — Saying measured for the first time: half of what it reads right it can say, the word records buy no coverage and cost up to 600 times the time, and a prediction of mine was wrong

**Objective** (the owner's word, "yes you can start it"). Reading is measured against the composer it replaced
(GRAMMAR-01: 21.8% strict, 42.4% senses aside against 16.1% / 33.6%). **Saying had no figure at all.** The one reply
path asks the grammar first (85), so what the grammar cannot say falls to the constructions taught, and what neither
says is a reply that admits it cannot say what it holds. This measures the first half of that: of the dev meanings the
grammar reads right whole, how many it says any sentence for, and whether the sentence it says first is the one the
meaning was read from.

**What can and cannot be scored.** `Grammar.say` returns only sentences that READ BACK to exactly the meaning asked
for, so "said and read back right" is not a score it can fail. What can: **coverage** (a meaning it says nothing for
is one it cannot put into words) and **exactness** (whether the gold sentence is first, or there at all).

### Two mistakes of mine, both measured rather than reasoned away

**(1) Saying cannot be measured from files, and the first run's figure was the harness's.** Measured files-only as
GRAMMAR-01 measures reading, the grammar said something for **5 of 394** meanings (1.3%) and what it said gives it
away: "Myself am from Russia." for "I am from Russia.", "Bill am to Japan." for "Bill was in Japan." **Cause:**
`HeldWords.words_for` returns `[]` when no `written_for` is passed (`grammar_words.py` line 737), and
`teaching_sources.file_words` passes none. What a thing is said WITH is memory's alone (`MemoryAgent.words_for`,
whose docstring is "What `Grammar.say` says a thing with"). Reading needs how words are USED, which files have;
saying needs which word NAMES a thing, which only memory holds. GRAMMAR-01 measures reading from files rightly, and
that is why the same harness cannot measure saying at all.

**(2) PREDICTED WRONG, written down before the run: that main, holding 0 word records and 0 sentences recorded
whole, would "say close to nothing, almost instantly".** It says exactly as many as the sandbox holding 559 records.
**Cause:** the last clause of `words_for`, which this entry's author had underweighted --
`if not found and self.name_of(folded, word_class) == folded` -- **a thing may be said by its own name**, which needs
only the word classes, and main holds 94,262 of them.

### What saying costs and covers (`on_store.py`, `SAY_BACK`, reads only)

The same 77 taught-word dev documents on both stores, the first 12 meanings each store reads right whole senses
aside said back. The two twelves overlap and are not identical, so coverage is a sample-level comparison; the timings
on the nine sentences both were asked are paired.

| | lyric_dev2 | main (lyric_db) |
|---|---|---|
| word records / sentences recorded whole | 559 / 6,137 | **0 / 0** |
| names the sentence records give | 5,137 | 0 |
| says any sentence at all | 6 of 12 (50.0%) | **6 of 12 (50.0%)** |
| the gold sentence first | 1 (8.3%) | 0 (0.0%) |
| the gold sentence at all | 3 (25.0%) | 1 (8.3%) |
| the twelve took | **504 s** | **120 s** |
| memory warm; reading the 77 | 279 s; 1 s | 138 s; 75 s |

**(3) The word-record layer buys no coverage for saying, buys a little exactness, and costs up to 600 times the
time.** Both stores say 6 of 12. The sandbox is better on exactness (the gold sentence first 1 against 0, among them
3 against 1), which is what more words for a thing should buy. The cost is the other way and it is not small, on the
sentences both were asked: **"I wash myself." 183.6 s on the sandbox against 0.3 s on main; "Your arm's broken."
267.2 s against 0.0 s; "Who stabbed Tom?" 49.8 s against 117.9 s.** A thing memory holds every form and every sense
of the class for is a thing the agenda combines every one of.

**(4) Saying is unbounded where it fails, by design, and that is where the time goes.** `Grammar.say` is anytime
realization (White 2004; Carroll and Oepen 2005): `while agenda and len(sentences) < SAID_AT_MOST` -- it stops at the
first 8 sentences that read back. A meaning it CAN say ends early (7 of the sandbox's 12 finished under 2 s). A
meaning it CANNOT say exhausts the whole agenda: 267 s to say nothing of "Your arm's broken.". The code records the
same shape priced at 238 words taught ("Who did Roy paint the box for?", over ten minutes, 2026-10-28); the sandbox
now holds 559.

**(5) Reading and saying are not in the same cost class.** The same warm store read 77 sentences in **1 s** (sandbox)
and spent **504 s** saying twelve of their meanings. On main, 75 s to read 77 and 120 s to say twelve.

**How the stall was found, since it cost the session an hour.** The first store run was launched piped through
`tail -40`, which holds every line until the process exits, so 44 minutes passed with an empty output file. CPU at
100%, memory flat at 3.6 GB, its Postgres connections idle 35 minutes: computing, not blocked. `py-spy dump` (root,
the owner ran it) put it in `Grammar.say` at `grammar.py:3356`, the chart's partner loop. **Fixed in the script, not
in a note:** the leg now prints every meaning's cost as it lands, and `SAY_BACK` bounds **how many meanings are
asked**, never how long the grammar may search -- a cap there would report an expensive meaning as "said nothing" and
hide the only thing worth seeing.

**For the re-teach.** (84) found main lacks three layers and this prices one of them for saying: **the word records
are not what saying is missing.** Adding them to main would buy exactness in single figures and make saying
dramatically slower. What saying is actually short of is coverage -- half of what the grammar reads right it cannot
say at all -- and that half is not explained by any layer measured here.

**What is NOT measured.** Only 12 meanings a store, and only the grammar: `derived_reader.say` falls back to the
constructions taught (628,380 on main) when the grammar says nothing, and whether they cover the half the grammar
misses is the other leg of the owner's run and is not done. Nor is what the constructions cost.

## 2026-10-29 (85) — The three lists settled into one register, and understanding audited: every kind of taught language reaches a reading but one

**Objective.** The owner's decision stands: **nothing is re-taught until teaching, learning and understanding — reading
and responding — are down packed.** (84) audited teaching and learning and left two things: a finding waiting on his
word (three lists of language tags that must agree and did not), and the larger half unaudited (whether each kind of
memory actually changes a reading, and responding). He settled the first — "settle the three lists then go into
understanding" — so both are here.

### Part 1 — The three lists are one register

**What was wrong.** Two things follow from a memory being taught language, and they were decided in two places with
two different lists: `MemoryFilter.EXEMPT_EVENT_TAGS` named fourteen kinds and kept each from being judged novel or
complex enough to keep; a set of three at `MemoryAgent._store_memory` kept a record of how English is used from being
read as a claim about the world. (A third, `_LANGUAGE_RECORDS`, named nine source_context fields for the same
decision — so four hand-written lists, not three.) `listening` was in the claim set and not the exemption table, so
the same memory was taught language to one and not the other.

**What it cost, measured rather than assumed.** The exposure was the reverse of what (84) guessed. `listening` is one
memory and a decline would have lost it, which is a risk and not a cost yet. The real cost was the other way: the
**eleven kinds the claim set left out were read whole by the grammar at every store**, and they claimed nothing.
Across both stores, **0 of 276,000+ taught-language memories carry a conclusion or claim facts** — 0 of 94,262 word
classes on main, 0 of 108,300 heard-after, 0 of 12,544 analysed sentences, 0 of 1,187 word classes and 6,137 sentence
records on the sandbox (`metadata ? 'conclusion'`, both stores, read-only). 576,981 memories on main do carry one, so
the column is the right one and the zeros are real. The same shape was priced before at a quarter-second a read
(0 claims in 30,505 of them, 2026-10-09).

**The fix.** One register, derived from the table that already names every kind and why it is one:
`MemoryFilter.TAUGHT_LANGUAGE_TAGS = frozenset(tag for tag, kind in EXEMPT_EVENT_TAGS.items() if kind == "taught
language")` — **15 kinds** with `listening` filed under it. One question asks it: `MemoryAgent.taught_language(tags,
source_context)`, which both sites call. A kind added to the table is decided once, which matters because every kind
is about to be taught again.

**Verified.** `admitted_proposition` and ordinary prose still read as claims (a register that grew to cover everything
a pass writes would silence the claims teaching exists to land — the same defect with the sign reversed), and
`tests/test_derived_reading.py` **126 pass** unchanged.

### Part 2 — Understanding: reading and responding

**How it was audited.** By the routes, not the comments. Every kind of taught language has exactly one read-back site
in `MemoryAgent` (`_rows_tagged(TAG)`), and the fifteen converge in one warm pass (`_rebuild_word_class_view`). From
each view, the question a reader asks for it was traced forward; the questions themselves were parsed out of the
reading and saying code rather than listed.

**What the readers ask for is five questions**, asked of memory by name in `core/semantics/derived_reader.py`:
`pattern_inventory`, `said_selection`, `grammar_view`, `listening_evidence`, `coarse_senses`; hearing and the voice
ask `stated_pronunciations` and `lessons_taught`; the conversation asks `grammar_view`, `word_classes`,
`word_meanings` and its own. **Most kinds reach a reading inside one of those answers, not by a question of their
own** — word groups and the sentences analysed by hand become the structure view, and the structure view is part of
`grammar_view`.

**(1) Fourteen of the fifteen kinds reach a reading.** `language_pattern`, `word_class`, `heard_after` and
`word_forms` through `pattern_inventory`; `said_of` through `said_selection`; `word_group`, `analysed_sentence`,
`taught_sentence`, `derived_sentence`, `sentence_record`, `word_record` and `read_english` through `grammar_view`;
`pronunciation` through `stated_pronunciations`.

**(2) The finding: `argued_sentence` reaches no reader. 10,495 of them are held on main and they change no reading.**
Which phrases are a happening's arguments is read back as `ArgumentStructureView` and handed to `CompositionView` —
**the composer that was replaced on 2026-10-20**, whose decisions where no remembered sentence looked like the
sentence were wrong one time in three (`core/semantics/grammar.py`, first paragraph: "the most specific situations
met decided 71% of what a word stands for, 2% wrong; the rest were decided by coarser ones, 9% to 75% wrong"). The
live path composes through `GrammarView.compose_sentence`; `agent.composition_view()` is called by nothing but the
refresh after learning and one test, and neither `grammar.py` nor `derived_reader.py` mentions an argument anywhere
(`grep -c argued` = 0 in both). **PropBank's role information does reach the grammar** — through the word records'
`joins`, built from the PropBank files when the record is made (`teaching_sources._propbank_joins`), not from these
memories. So for the re-teach: **re-teaching the argued sentences changes no reading; re-teaching the word records
does.** Whether to wire the arguments into the grammar is a behaviour change and the owner's call.

**(3) Responding is one path and it is fed by the same taught language.** `Conversation.say(understanding)` — "THE
substrate's reply — the one path from what it holds to what it says" — renders every held fact through `_said` /
`_said_rule`, which call `derived_reader.say`. That **asks the grammar first** (`GrammarView.say`: the grammar a
sentence is read by, used the other way) **and the constructions taught second** (`_said_whole`). So what is said
changes with what was taught, through both. The alternative is on the record where it happened: there used to be a
`natural_reply()` beside it and an `or` between them that fell through to an introspection dump for every question
that was not a yes/no.

**(4) The knowledge half is inside reading AND saying, and what it needs is a re-teach requirement, not a
wiring gap.** The first version of this entry said "reading depends on the knowledge half, not only the language
half" in a place that read as if responding did not have it. It does, twice over. **The content of a reply IS the
knowledge half**: `Understanding.known` is the concepts resolved against the store (`informative`), beside recall,
what things mean as the word records say it (`meanings`), and what held facts point at (`pointed_at`) — all gathered
in `understand()`, which the field comments say is where the database is needed because "`say()` is a pure function
over what was already found". **And reading and saying are one object**: `GrammarView.read` and `GrammarView.say` are
two methods on the one cached view (`memory_agent._grammar_view`, built once a warm), and that view is constructed
with `GraphKnowledge` from `unified.concept_relations` — each thing's kinds (`isa`), what particular ones are
(`instance of`), and for a thing held as a kind of nothing what its definition is written with. **148,843 links on
main.** A link stored reaches the live view at once, without waiting for a warm (`memory_agent` line 3609:
`self._grammar_view.words.hear_kind(...)`).

What is actually at stake is the **order of the re-teach**: no language lesson writes `isa` or `instance of` — the
propositions do. So re-teaching the fifteen language layers alone gives the grammar nothing new about what things
are, and it asks that of every word it reads.

**(5) The listening memory holds no counts, by design, and a store-level check says it is empty.** Asked whether every
memory of each kind carries the key its reader reads, every kind answered 100% — 108,300 of 108,300, 94,262 of 94,262,
and so on — except `listening`, 0 of 1. That is not a defect: the counts are **beliefs the one memory is named by**
(`derived_reader._held_listening_counts` reads them from the uncertainty system), weighed by `weighed()` when a
sentence reads more than one way. Worth recording because the store-level check finds nothing and the code is the only
place that says why.

**Built: `tests/test_understanding_reaches_the_reader.py` (5 tests).** Every kind of taught language is recorded with
the question it reaches a reading through, or recorded in `NOT_ASKED` with what is known about why it reaches
nothing; the questions are read out of the readers themselves, so a reader that stops asking takes down every kind
that reached a reading through it. The `NOT_ASKED` test **fails both ways on purpose**: stale if the view stops
existing, and failing if a reader starts asking for it, which says the finding is fixed and belongs in `ANSWERS`.
With the rewritten `tests/test_language_tags_agree.py` (8, holding the derivation instead of being a fourth copy of
the list) and (83)–(84)'s, **24 pass**; `tests/test_memory_worthiness_semantics.py` and
`tests/test_sentence_records.py` with them, **72 pass**; `tests/test_derived_reading.py` **126 pass**.

**What is NOT verified, said plainly.** This audits the **wiring**: that each kind of memory reaches a reader, and
which one. It does **not** measure what each kind is worth to a reading — only `word_group` has that figure here
(`GROUPS-01`, `STRUCTURE-03`: nearly a point on EWT dev and PUD, 0.6 on GUM's held-out test). Reading a sentence
better with a kind than without it is a measurement per kind, against the 911-document split, and it is not done.

## 2026-10-29 (84) — The teaching and learning path audited before the re-teach: complete, and held complete by what it was missing

**Objective.** The owner's decision: **nothing is re-taught until teaching, learning and understanding — reading and
responding — are down packed.** (83) made a run report everything it wrote. This asks the next question of the same
shape: does a source's lesson reach memory at all? A capability a source offers that no pass asks for is teaching
that silently does not happen, which is the one failure a re-teach cannot survive, because the run would report
success for the part that ran and say nothing of the part that never did.

**How it was audited.** Not by reading the comments: by reading the code and diffing what it says against what it
does. For each of the **17 teaching sources**, every public method needing no argument but itself is something a
pass could ask for; the names `TeachingPass.run` consumes were parsed out of the pass itself rather than listed by
hand, so the audit cannot inherit the same staleness it is looking for.

**Finding 1: the pass's dispatch is a hand-written list of method names, and it is complete.** `run` names seven in
a tuple (`argued`, `taught_sentences`, `word_groups`, `word_forms`, `derived`, `word_records`, `sentence_records`)
and seven more each on its own (`records`, `word_classes`, `usage`, `listening_pairs`, `analysed`, `said_of`,
`pronunciations`), sixteen names in all. Diffed against all 17 sources: **nothing a source can teach goes
unasked.** Four methods looked orphaned and are not — `definitions`, `senses` and `held_out` are constructor
attributes rather than methods, and `use_of` takes arguments and is called five times inside the source. Two more
are helpers and say so: `WikidataSource.sections` lists a cache's sections so the command line can name one, and
`WordNetSource.stated_senses` is read by that source's own `records()`.

**Finding 2, and it is a real one: a source prices everything it states, or prices each record, and nothing said
so.** Everything but `records()` is taught at `float(self.source.quality)` — one price for the whole of what a
source states. **ConceptNet has no such price and declares none**, instance or class: its weights run 0.5 to 4.47
on one relation, so every record carries its own (`quality_from_corroboration`). That is right, and it holds only
while ConceptNet teaches through `records()` alone. Grown a `usage()` or a `said_of()`, the pass would reach
`float(self.source.quality)` and raise `AttributeError` **partway through a pass that had already written** — the
failure arriving after the writing, which is the worst place for it. `LessonSource` also declares none at class
level and sets it per instance from the lesson file it reads, which is sound. The contract is now written down as
the thing that checks it.

**Finding 3: the learning half is one path, and it holds.** The seven kinds of language held whole all go through
`_learn_held`, which dispatches on two strings per call — a `MemoryAgent` method name and a ledger `subject_kind`.
Checked: **all seven method names resolve** on `MemoryAgent`, and **all seven subject kinds are tags the store
really holds** (`argued_sentence` 10,495 on main, `derived_sentence` 8,679, `taught_sentence` 9,874, `word_forms`
3,703; `sentence_record`, `word_record` and `word_group` 0, because main was never taught them). The memory agent
is the sole writer, an item memory refuses is counted refused and the reason logged, and no belief or domain is
made of language. Nothing here accepts items and drops them.

**Finding 4, the one left open for a decision: three lists of language tags must agree about the same memory, and
they disagree.** Taught language is how to read and how to say, never something Lyric knows, and three places carry
that distinction — `MemoryAgent`'s 23 `*_TAG` constants, `MemoryFilter.EXEMPT_EVENT_TAGS` (14 language tags, which
keeps a lesson from being judged novel enough to keep), and a set of three at `memory_agent._store_memory` (which keeps
a record of how English is used from being read as a claim). **`listening` is in the third and not the second.** Its
exposure is one memory — the one the listener's counts are beliefs about — so the cost today is nil, and the shape
is what matters: each of these lists has fallen behind at least once and every time the cost was measured. The
treebank's structure pass stopped on one declined sentence (2026-10-16); word classes and pronunciations were
declined and counted as skipped, silently; **53 of the 59 memories handed to reasoning for UNDERSTANDS-PROSE-01 and
-02 were examples of English**, so "Is seven odd?" was answered with "'seven' is used as an adjective." (2026-10-23);
and the word "wall"'s record was read as a claim by the grammar, 109 million combinations and 148 seconds
(TRAIN-FORMAT-02, 2026-10-26). **One list, derived, in place of three kept by hand is the fix**, and it is a change
to how memory is classified, so it waits on the owner.

**Finding 5, for the re-teach itself: main lacks three layers, not one.** Of the kinds a full teach produces, `
lyric_db` holds **0 word records, 0 sentences recorded whole and 0 word groups**. (82) priced the first; the other
two have never been counted.

**Built: three guards, because every finding here was a list kept by hand with nothing to make it fail.**
`tests/test_teaching_path.py` — everything a source can teach is asked for by the pass, with a reason required for
anything excluded and a check that each reason still names a method some source has; and the pricing contract of
finding 2. `tests/test_language_tags_agree.py` — every kind of taught language is exempt from being judged worth
keeping, is named by a tag constant, and every tag constant is decided about one way or the other, so a kind added
to `MemoryAgent` fails the test until someone says which it is. With (83)'s `tests/test_teach_snapshot.py`,
**16 pass**.

**What is NOT audited yet, said plainly.** This covers teaching and learning: that a lesson reaches memory and is
counted. It does **not** cover understanding. What was checked of reading is only that each kind of memory is named
somewhere outside the learning code, and the module that named all fourteen turned out to be the exemption list
above, not a reader. **Whether each kind of memory actually changes a reading is unverified**, and so is responding
(`say()`). That is the next piece of this audit and it is the larger half.

## 2026-10-29 (83) — A teaching run reports everything it wrote: the snapshot asks the store what it holds instead of naming eight things

**Objective.** The owner's point, said again and taken as the standing requirement: the work is to standardize
teaching and learning so that it does what it is meant to, because **everything is going to be re-taught**. What is
currently in a database is beside that point. A re-teach that cannot be verified from the run's own report is not a
re-teach anyone can trust, and (82) had just shown a run writing 1,107 word classes and reporting zeros in every
column.

**The defect, and its cause.** `scripts/teach.py`'s `snapshot()` named eight things — concepts, relations, beliefs,
domains, memberships, taught statements, words recorded, sentences recorded — each as its own `COUNT(*)`. Word
classes were not among them, and neither were language patterns (628,380 held), `said_of` (28,792), analysed,
argued, taught and derived sentences (12,544, 10,495, 9,874, 8,679), word forms (3,703), `heard_after` (108,300) or
thirty-odd other kinds. The cause is the shape and not the omission: **a list of kinds written in the reporting
script goes stale the moment a kind of learning is added**, and nothing makes it fail when it does. It had gone
stale silently, so a classes-only pass was honest in its pass report (`word classes: {'told': 1107, ...}`) and
blind in its substrate table, and the only way to prove the work was to count rows in the database by hand.

**Built: the store is asked what it holds.** `snapshot()` now counts, in two questions,

- **every kind of memory under the tag it is held by**, hot and cold together (`memory_hot` and `memory_cold`, so a
  memory tiered between them is not read as one that went missing), and
- **every table of the schemas memory is held in** (`unified`, `memory_hot`, `memory_cold`), named from the store's
  own catalogue, counting only tables holding rows themselves (`relkind = 'r'`), so a partitioned table is counted
  in its parts and not twice over.

On the main store that is **387 things — 47 kinds of memory and 340 tables — counted exactly in 0.73s**, of which 95
hold anything. A kind of learning added later is counted with nothing here touched again. The five tables the old
snapshot reported are all still counted and so are its three tags, so nothing it said was lost: it said eight things
of 387.

**And the report shows what moved.** The run printed all eight rows whether they moved or not; it now prints the
kinds and tables whose counts the run changed, kinds first and tables after (`what_moved`), and where none moved it
says so in words — "nothing moved: every kind of memory and every table it is held in holds what it held before" —
which is a result and not an empty table. A kind the store held **none** of before the run is in the after and not
in the before, so it is reported from nothing: that is the case the old snapshot could not report at all, and it is
the case every first re-teach of a kind will be.

**The other half of the same defect, guarded and not rewritten.** `Report.lines()` in `core/learning/teaching.py`
is also a hand-written list, of 17 lines over a dataclass of 24 fields. Checked: it names **all 24**, so a pass does
report everything it did today. What it lacked was anything to keep that true, so a field added without a line would
be learning performed and not reported — the same defect in the same place. A test now holds the property instead of
the report being rebuilt, which keeps the labels a reader of a run actually reads.

**Verified** (`tests/test_teach_snapshot.py`, 6 pass, `./venv_lyric/bin/python3`): every tag the store answers with
is counted, including one whose name appears nowhere in the code; the five tables the old snapshot reported are all
still counted; cold memory is in the question asked; a kind written for the first time is shown from nothing; what
held still is not reported; kinds sort before tables; nothing taught moves nothing; and every field of a pass report
reaches the lines it prints. The new `snapshot()` was also run against `lyric_db` itself, reads only, and returned
the 387 counts above with `word_class` at 94,262 — the number (82) had to count by hand.

**Removed.** `_count`, the one-row helper the eight questions used, now that nothing calls it.

**What this is for.** It is not a measurement and it moves no reading score. It is the instrument the re-teach will
be read through: whatever is taught next, the run says what memory gained, by kind, in its own words, without anyone
having to know in advance which kinds to ask about.

## 2026-10-29 (81) — The vocabulary floor: the class lessons state a quality and an adverb of several words

**Objective.** (80) put the vocabulary floor first in the order of work, and (79) built a reading for several words
that are one word of whatever kind memory holds them as. The owner asked what main holds and whether it has to be
re-taught. So: find what main lacks, and make the lessons state it.

**What main holds.** Not a re-teach — a layer it was never taught. `lyric_db` holds 0 word records, 0 sentence
records, 12,544 analysed sentences, 8,679 derivations, 9,874 taught sentences, 148,843 links. Word by word, the
class lessons of (73) did their job: "chained" and "developed" are held as adjectives (a second class on a single
word), "grow up" and "take off" as verbs of several words, and "credit card" and "prime minister" arrive through the
words of their facts. But main holds **nothing at all** for "fed up", "in vain", "at last" or "disco music".

**The cause, one line.** `WordNetSource._word_classes` stated a word of several words only where it was a verb:

```python
if len(parts) > 1 and word_class != "VERB":
    continue
```

The reason given was that a noun of several words is said with its facts ("A credit card is a card."), which name
it. Main proves that half-true: it works for "credit card", fails for "disco music", and **can never work for a
quality or an adverb**, because neither has a fact to be named in. So (79)'s reading of a quality or an adverb of
several words was unreachable on main, whatever it was taught.

**Built.** The lessons state a verb, a quality and an adverb of several words; a noun's words are still named by its
facts. WordNet holds 2,776 verbs of letters, 483 qualities and 704 adverbs, against 58,597 nouns — fifty times the
qualities and adverbs together, whose own measurement this is not.

**The error the first version made, and its cause.** Taught to lyric_dev2 whole (1,187 pairs, 1,142 words, all told,
none skipped), the lessons **lost a sentence**: GRAMMAR-01's eight sets 120 right whole of 231 to 119, the 77 50 to
49. The cause was one word. WordNet holds "to it" as a lemma of `thereto.r.01`, so "I'm totally indifferent to it."
read `instance_of(?v2, to it)`. A pronoun stands for whatever was spoken of, so words holding one are not one word,
which means the same wherever it is said — and WordNet holds 33 such qualities and 47 such adverbs ("on it", "under
it", "as it is", "in his own right", and 22 of them "one hundred" and the numbers built on it, which the grammar
reads as the number they are). The lessons state none of them now. Said of the lessons and not of the reading,
because a noun of several words may hold a pronoun and keep its own word ("coal mine", "gold mine"), and a verb's
"it" can be frozen into the verb ("get it" is to understand, "call it a day"): the 43 verbs WordNet holds so have
been stated since (73) and are left exactly as they were, so this states more and nothing less.

**Research** (`GRAMMAR-01/diagnostics/several_classes.py`, new, files only): what this vocabulary calls one word and
how many of them are. Over the 1,194 dev documents it calls 63 runs of two or three words one word and 27 are one
concept (43%), qualities 14 of 22 and adverbs 13 of 41; over the 9,552 train documents 637 runs and 233 (37%). It is
noisy, and what it calls wrongly most is a handful of words the grammar reads otherwise: "a lot" 45, "out of" 42,
"used to" 37, "at all" 29, "kind of" 28, "a few" 20. What keeps that honest is that the grammar **weighs** an entry
against the words apart and does not take it — "kind of" before a noun is the grammar's own (`subkind`, (75)), and
of the 10 dev runs of "kind of" counted wrong here the kind_of set moved not at all.

**Measured** (lyric_dev2, 231 documents over the eight sets, 559 word records; the run with the pronoun words hidden
at the asking, because a stated class cannot be taken back and they were taught before the rule was found):

| by their words, pronouns as unknowns | right whole | facts F1 |
|---|---|---|
| before the lessons | 120 of 231 (51.9%) | 75.0% |
| the lessons as first written | 119 of 231 (51.5%) | 74.9% |
| the lessons with the pronoun rule | 120 of 231 (51.9%) | 75.1% |

Every set at or above where it was, nothing lost, `precedes` one more fact right and `instance_of` four fewer wrong,
against three more `has_property` facts read and none more right. **On this store the lessons change nothing**, and
that is what they should: the 75 words these sets need were taught to lyric_dev2 by hand in (79), so the lessons add
only the vocabulary beyond them. The floor they lay is for main, which holds none of it.

**The capability without any teaching at all** (the files-only reader, WordNet as its word memory, which is what
main becomes once the lessons are run): "I'm fed up with math." `has_property(?speaker, fed up)`, "At last, we
arrived in California." `has_property(?v0, at last)`, "The book is out of print." `has_property(?v0, out of print)`,
"Tom is kind of tall." `has_property(?v0, kind of)`. Four of five right with nothing taught. The fifth is the rule's
window: it asks memory for runs of three words and two, so "All of a sudden it rained." splits into `all` and `of a
sudden`. That is 4 of the dev split's 13 adverbs of several words, and its own measured change.

**The dev split's reach**, for what this is worth against what is left (`several_words.py dev`, 1,194 documents):
168 names of several words, 79 nouns, 31 verbs, **12 qualities, 13 adverbs**. The qualities and adverbs are 25
concepts, and WordNet spells every one of them; the 79 nouns it spells 98.7% of and states none of.

**The cost of a word record, measured** (the other layer main holds none of): the first costs 446s because the
sources load, each after it **0.09s**. So 3,919 records (the treebank's words said five times or more) is six
minutes of building, 9,387 (every treebank word WordNet knows) fourteen minutes, and all 147,306 WordNet lemmas
under four hours. This is cheaper than it was thought by two orders of magnitude, so the vocabulary is not the
obstacle the sizing was expected to show.

**Where it stands.** lyric_dev2's 231 documents 120 right whole (51.9%), the 77 50 of 77 (65%), facts F1 75.1%; the
bar 95%. Main unchanged and unmeasured against this: the owner runs `--source wordnet-classes` on lyric_db (additive,
a class taught already is not taught again), and then main is measured with the error budget for the first honest
baseline of the real store. After that the order of (80) stands: which word takes which (`prose_joins.py` 68.0%, the
structure view 72.5% on the same test), then a verb's places, then which kind a thing is.

## 2026-10-29 (80) — The error budget: where the distance to the bar actually is

**Objective.** Nine sessions have closed one error group each and moved the 77 from 35 right to 50. The owner asked
what it would take to reach the bar. Closing groups one at a time cannot answer that, because it never says how much
of the distance each group is. So: take the false errors out of the measure, then measure the whole of it.

**The measure's false errors.** Two, both found by reading the group's remaining failures in (79), both of them the
measure or the reader naming a thing and not the reading being wrong:

- A word of several words was not a word of the sentence. `words_of_sentence` counted every run of two and three
  words **as written** and not the word the run is a form of, where it counts a word of one that way and a hyphened
  word in each of its spellings ((72)). So a thing the gold says by a word of several words could be named by no
  word of the sentence at all: "Tom took off his bullet-proof vest." has the gold's `take_off.v.06` (named `undress
  take off`) against the reading's `take_off.v.02` (named `take off`), and the sentence says neither — it says "took
  off". The reading read "took off" as one verb, which the gold does too, and was scored wrong for it.
- A compound was named by the first word and the second's **sense name**: "cell phone" was `cell telephone`, which
  is no thing's name and no words of the sentence. Named by its own words now, the second as the word it is a form
  of ("dairy products" `dairy product`).

Of the eight sets one sentence changed and none was lost. The records and the measure's sense table were checked
against each other over the 163 senses of the words taught this week and agree on every one, so this was not a
record defect; and of the gold's 4,268 concepts the table has no name at all for 48 (1.1%), which is the measure's
own floor.

**Measured** (`on_store.py` now prints the error budget; lyric_dev2, the whole dev split, 911 documents with a gold
meaning, read by their words with pronouns as unknowns): 465 right whole (51.0%), facts 2,922 of 3,981 (73.4%).

| the link said | gold | missed | recall | of all missed | cumulative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `instance_of` (which kind a thing is) | 1,366 | 270 | 80.2% | 25.5% | 25.5% |
| `done_by` | 627 | 166 | 73.5% | 15.7% | 41.2% |
| `done_to` | 451 | 125 | 72.3% | 11.8% | 53.0% |
| `has_property` | 313 | 95 | 69.6% | 9.0% | 61.9% |
| `precedes` | 371 | 79 | 78.7% | 7.5% | 69.4% |
| `located_in` | 73 | 31 | 57.5% | 2.9% | 72.3% |
| `creates` | 32 | 25 | 21.9% | 2.4% | 74.7% |
| `part_of` | 52 | 24 | 53.8% | 2.3% | 77.0% |
| `during` | 111 | 24 | 78.4% | 2.3% | 79.2% |
| `comes_from` | 27 | 23 | 14.8% | 2.2% | 81.4% |

**Three findings, and they change what to work on.**

1. **The five commonest links hold 69% of every missed fact**, and none of them is exotic: which kind a thing is,
   who does it, what it is done to, what quality it has, that it happened before now. Each is at 70% to 80% where
   99% is wanted.
2. **The links the last nine sessions built rules for are rounding error.** `comes_from` is 27 facts of 3,981,
   `creates` 32, `part_of` 52, `state_of` 14, `received_by` 16 — together under 5% of the budget. Every one was a
   real defect and worth fixing; none of them was ever going to move the bar.
3. **Errors cascade; they are not near misses.** A wrong sentence is missing **2.37 of the 4.4 facts it says**. Were
   the facts decided apart, 73.4% each would give 25.9% of sentences right; 55.8% are right, so the facts of a
   sentence stand or fall together. One structural decision — which word takes which — carries two or three facts,
   which is why the whole-sentence figure is so much better than chance and why a wrong sentence is wrong about most
   of itself.

**What the ceilings say about the bar.** Taking the best way measured for each place (`verb_places.py`, (77)): a
verb's subject 92.7%, its object 86.8%, a second object 89.7%, a preposition's link 45.1%, a passive's subject ~44%
(the gold itself split 49/42), a passive's "by" 8.8%. Lifting `instance_of`, `has_property` and `precedes` to 90-95%
and the places to those ceilings gives about 3,364 of 3,981 facts, 84.5%, which at the correlation observed here is
roughly three sentences in four. **Hitting every ceiling we have measured does not reach 95%.** The bar needs
evidence the reader does not have yet, and the plainest candidate is how little it has read: 12,544 sentences is a
small thing to count "what goes with what" from.

**Where it stands.** The 77 by their words 50 (65%); the whole dev split 465 of 911 (51.0%), facts 73.4%; the bar
95%. The order of work the budget gives, largest first: the vocabulary floor (the owner's WordNet class lessons,
which end the "no entry offered" family the last four sessions each chipped at), then which word takes which
(`prose_joins.py`: 68.0% of content words joined as the analysis by hand does, Lyric's own structure view 72.5% on
the same test), then a verb's places, then which kind a thing is. The small links are done being worth a session
each.

## 2026-10-29 (79) — Several words that are one word: read as whatever kind memory holds them as

**Objective.** The 77's next group by size as (78) counted it: a noun or name of several words (6 of the 28 left).

**Research first** (`GRAMMAR-01/diagnostics/several_words.py`, files only: every concept of the PMB's 9,552 gold
train documents whose own words are several — the words of its span no tighter span covers and the line does not mark
as words of the grammar — against every run of words the sentences say, which is what a way of deciding must not call
one concept). Two kinds are told apart, because only the first is a word of the language: one the line names with a
`Name` of several words or WordNet's own sense spells as one of its lemmas, and one the annotation lumps ("Call
again." `call.v.03`, "insured with" `insure.v.03`, "ten o'clock" `time.n.08`: 663 of them, not counted below).

| one word of several | of them | a capitalised run catches | WordNet spells it so |
|---|---|---|---|
| a name ("New York", "Second World War") | 420 | 77.6% | 45.5% |
| a thing ("hair dryer", "red wine") | 747 | 0% | **100%** |
| a verb ("split up", "picked up", "ran into") | 238 | 0% | **100%** |
| an adverb ("in vain", "out of the blue") | 105 | 0% | **100%** |
| a quality ("fed up", "in love") | 76 | 0% | **100%** |

WordNet spells every one of the 1,166 that are not names as one word, in one of three spellings (as written 97.8% of
the things, the last word as its base 11.7%, run together 8.8%) — so **memory taught from WordNet holds them all**,
and what `GraphKnowledge.known_name` asks for is there to be had. Against that, of the 44,993 runs of two words the
sentences say only 3.7% are one concept: WordNet as written calls 1,852 one and 58.6% are, the last word's base 122
and 81.1% are, run together 753 and 14.1% are, a capitalised run 487 and 61.2% are.

The verbs were counted 31 at first and 238 once two things were put right, both of them the gold's spelling and not
the language's: a verb's particle is marked as a word of the sentence's grammar, so "filled *out*" left one word
behind, and a verb of several words carries its form on the first word where WordNet spells the base ("filled out"
`fill_out.v.03`, "fell in love" `fall_in_love.v.01`). Memory needs neither correction, holding the forms of a word of
several words as it holds a word's ("grew up" under `grow up`, `WordRecord.forms`).

**Cause.** Read on lyric_dev2, the six of (78)'s count are not one thing and only three of them are this group:
"prime minister" is held as one word already, its entry the surest at the word (-0.35), and the sentence fails on
"Who is the Hungarian prime minister?" read as a request; "IKEA furniture" is a name right before a thing; "Phobos
and Deimos" names in a list after a colon. Of the three that are:

- **The words were missing, and the rule offered a thing alone.** "I like disco music." already reads one concept of
  both words, by the rule for a noun before a noun, and names it by its words ("disco music") because memory holds no
  record of the word; the gold's name is `disco` (`disco_music.n.01`). And a quality, an adverb or a verb of several
  words was never offered at all: `Lexicon._together`'s "words memory knows as one thing" made a NOUN entry and
  nothing else, so "fed up", "in vain", "at last" were read as their words apart.
- **The verb of several words was asked for under the wrong word.** The verb-and-particle rule asks memory
  `known_verb([the verb's name, the particle])`, and a verb's name is the thing's and not the word's: "grow" is
  `cultivate grow`, "show" is `to show`, so `known_verb(['cultivate grow', 'up'])` is nothing where
  `known_verb(['grow', 'up'])` is `grow up`. It worked only where a verb's name happens to be the word ("let up").
  That is why "Where did Golda Meir grow up?" read no whole at all.
- **A run opening with a capital was never asked for.** The rule wanted every word of the run written lowercase, so
  "Easter egg" and "At last, we arrived in California." were not asked of memory, which holds both.

**Built.** `Lexicon._together` asks memory what it holds several words as (`Words.known_words`, `Knowledge`,
`MemoryAgent._held_names`: each kind of word memory holds them as, with the name it holds them under, in place of the
two questions `known_name`/`known_verb` asked of one class each) and offers that kind's entries — a thing, a quality,
an adverb, as sure as its words are. A verb of several words is still read by the verb and its particle, which says
the form and the frame too, and that is asked under the words as written as well as under the verb's name. The run
may open with a capital, its later words lowercase telling it from a name of several words. And it is asked with the
last word as the word it is a form of ("gold medals" `gold medal`, "sleeping pills" `sleeping pill`), the spelling of
the best precision measured (81.1%).

**Taught** (lyric_dev2): the 75 words of several words the set says that it held no record of, recorded whole
(`word_record_of`): 48 things, 8 adverbs, 4 qualities, 7 verbs and the rest several kinds. None refused; no concept,
belief or domain made. Word records 484 -> 559.

**Measured** (lyric_dev2, all eight sets in one run, by their words with pronouns as unknowns). The new set is
`several_words_test.json`, the 101 dev documents whose gold makes one concept of several words that is not a name:
61 things, 25 verbs, 11 qualities, 9 adverbs.

| by their words, lyric_dev2 | the store and code of (78) | the 75 words taught | and the rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| several words (new) | 13 of 87 (F1 45.6%) | 37 of 101 (60.1%) | **44 of 101 (65.6%)** |
| the 77 | 49 (F1 84.1%) | 50 (84.6%) | 50 (84.6%) |
| hyphen (15) | 6 | 6 | 5 |
| degree 13 / denial 6 / kind of 5 / clock 6 / participle 9 | | the same | the same |

The set grew from 87 documents to 101 when the gold's spelling of a verb of several words was put right, so the first
column is the smaller set; measured on the 87 with the words taught and the rule in its first form it was 38 (62.5%).
The rule alone, before the words were taught, moved nothing at all on any set, which is the point of the two columns:
lyric_dev2 held a record for one of these 76 words ("prime minister"), and a rule that asks memory what it holds
several words as has nothing to answer until memory holds them.

Eight sentences became right by the rule — "I'm fed up.", "I'm fed up with math.", "Is Tom all right?", "You are in
love with him.", "Tom never quarrels with his wife in public.", "At last, we arrived in California.", "I'm painting
an Easter egg.", "I waited for hours, but she didn't show up." — and one became wrong: **"Tom took off his
bullet-proof vest."** It now reads "took off" as one verb, which the gold does too (`take_off.v.06`), and names it
`take off` where the gold's sense is named `undress take off`: the reading picks another sense of the verb of several
words. The measure cannot reconcile them, because a thing is named by the word of the sentence it is a sense of
(`named_by_their_words`) and the sentence says "took off" while the lemma is `take_off` — `words_of_sentence` counts
every two and three words side by side as written and not the word they are a form of. Before the change the reading
read "took" alone, named it `undress take off` and read "off" as a preposition saying nothing, which the measure
scored right. The reading is better and the score is worse.

**Found, not fixed.** A name of several words. 252 of the gold's 420 (60.0%) are runs whose words the treebank writes
as something other than a name ("the European Constitution": "European" an adjective 26 times, "Constitution" a
noun); only 74 (17.6%) have every word written as a name. And a capitalised run is as likely to be one name either
way — of the two-word runs it calls one, 59.1% are where the words are written otherwise against 68.5% where they are
written as names, against a 3.7% base rate. The grammar scores a run as sure as each of its words is held a name, so
"the European Constitution" is offered at -4.97 against -0.35 for the two words apart, and loses. What the
measurement does not give is a score to put in its place that is not a constant of its own, so nothing was built.

A verb of several words WordNet spells as one word: "fist fighting" is `fistfight.v.01`, lemma `fistfight`, so no
spelling of the two words finds it, and running the words together calls 753 two-word runs one concept of which only
14.1% are.

A quality of several words beginning with a preposition is offered and outscored: "I've fallen in love with you."
offers "in love" (`enamored`, -0.52) against "in" a preposition (-0.19) and "love" a thing (-0.34).

A name right before a thing ("Do you like IKEA furniture?", the gold `creates`): of 1,574 such places the gold makes
44.1% one concept or no two things, 44.3% no link at all, then `comes_from` 3.9%, `has_member` 3.1%, `part_of` 1.5%,
`owned_by` 1.5%, `creates` 0.8%. No link is the commonest reading; the reader's `received_by` is none of them.

**Where it stands.** The 77 by their words: lyric_dev2 50 of 77 (65%), main 40 (52%, not re-run);
the bar is 95%. Several words that are one word of the language read as one word of the kind memory holds them as,
where memory holds them — which, the measurement says, is every one of the 1,166 that are not names, once it is
taught them. Names of several words are left as they were, and are the biggest single thing known and not built.

**The 77's 27 left, counted by cause** (each sentence under the one thing that would have to change):

| | |
|---|---|
| single cases | 9: "Ain't", "off duty", "novel-based", a gerund with a possessive, a fronted "By whom", "kind of" with what is asked, "since" with the sense of "took", "including", and the quoted pair that reads no whole |
| which link a word says | 5: a verb's place 3 ("Nobody called him." `received_by`, "Our bus collided with a truck." the Co-Theme, "Caesar falls" `done_to`), a possessive 1 ("Boeing's headquarters" `part_of`), a time with "at" 1 |
| the reading says more than the gold | 2: a past said ("You reek of alcohol."), a name equated with the name said of it |
| a place or people's adjective | 2: "a Norwegian town" `part_of`, "a Lesbian poet" from Lesbos |
| the one participant said to do it | 2: the horse ridden, the tennis played |
| several words that are one word | 2: "fist fighting", "European Constitution" |
| a bare plural | 1: "Are anal fissures curable?" read as the kind itself |
| a name right before a thing | 1: "Do you like IKEA furniture?" |
| names in a list after a colon | 1: "Mars has two moons: Phobos and Deimos." |
| a question read as a request | 1: "Who is the Hungarian prime minister?" |
| what a later word refers to | 1: "Tom chased the mugger and caught him." |

(78) counted this group 6 and it is 2: three of its six were other things, and "disco music" is right now.

Next by size: single cases aside, which link a word says — five sentences, three of them a verb's place, which

## 2026-10-29 (78) — Participles: a quality where memory holds the word as one, and an Experiencer beside a doer is what it is done to

**Objective.** The 77's next group by size (lab notebook (77)): participles read as passives or verbs ("Is the dog
chained?", "Israel is a developed country.", "Riding a horse is really thrilling.", "I've been stung by a hornet.").

**Cause.** Read on lyric_dev2, the four show two, and neither is a rule of the grammar:
- **Nothing offered the quality.** A word's ways are the classes memory holds it as and the uses the sentences it has
  read gave it (`Lexicon._evidence`, `HeldWords._uses_of`). An adjective spelled as a participle is a word of its own
  in WordNet (`chained.s.01`, `thrilling.s.02`, `developed.a.02`), and lyric_dev2 held a record for "chain" and none
  for "chained": of "chained" it held one class, VERB, by the rule that a word spelled as a form of a verb is one. So
  every entry for "chained" was the verb's, and "Is the dog chained?" was read as a chaining with the dog joined to
  nothing (`ask: given instance_of(?v0, dog) & instance_of(?v1, arrange chain)`), "Israel is a developed country." as
  a developing done to Israel, "really thrilling" as a thrilling happening, done by the riding. Where the classes come
  from WordNet for every spelling (GRAMMAR-01's files; main, taught WordNet's class lessons whole in (73)), the same
  grammar reads the first two right: of the six documents of the new participle set main had already read, main read
  five right and lyric_dev2 two.
- **An Experiencer said beside a doer.** "I've been stung by a hornet." was read `done_by` the speaker and `done_by`
  the hornet, which is what lyric_dev2 was taught: the PMB writes the stung person an Experiencer ("I was stung by a
  bee.", "Tom was stung by a bee.", "I got stung by a bee.", all three held), `HAPPENING_ROLES` linked every
  Experiencer `done_by`, and so the passive's subject taught `done_by`. The dev sentence's gold writes a Patient.

**Research first** (`GRAMMAR-01/diagnostics/participles.py`: each word of the PMB's 9,552 gold train documents written
as a participle or an -ing form, standing where either a quality or a doing may stand, against what the gold says it
is; a word after a thing is not counted, no spelling telling the sentence's own verb from a thing's participle):

| where it stands | the gold says a quality | an adjective sense spelled so catches | of what it calls qualities, are | the treebank's adjective catches | of what it calls, are |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| after a form of "be", -ed (664) | 179 (27%) | 95.5% | 36.6% | 57.0% | 74.5% |
| after a form of "be", -ing (614) | 13 (2%) | 100% | 6.0% | 61.5% | 33.3% |
| before a noun, -ed (40) | 27 (68%) | 96.3% | 89.7% | 66.7% | 94.7% |
| before a noun, -ing (74) | 4 (5%) | 100% | 28.6% | 50.0% | 40.0% |
| after "been", -ed (45) | 2 (4%) | 100% | 11.1% | 50.0% | 50.0% |
| opening, -ing (19) | 8 (42%) | 100% | 88.9% | 0% | |

The sense says whether the word may be a quality (95% of the gold's are of a word WordNet holds as an adjective), and
how often the word is written as an adjective says whether it is one here (74% to 95% of what that calls a quality is
one). That is what the grammar does with a word memory holds: the entry is offered because memory holds the class,
and weighed by how often the word is used that way. Nothing to build in the reader; the words were missing.

And the Experiencer, counted over the gold: 45 documents say an Experiencer beside a doer, every one of them the one
affected ("The tiger licked him.", "She pinched him.", "Tom patted himself on the back.", "I was stung by a bee.");
766 say an Experiencer alone, who experiences it ("I envy you.", "Mary bores me.").

**Built.** `pmb_meanings.happening_link`: the link a happening's role makes beside the roles said with it — a Theme
alone who does it (as before), an Experiencer beside a doer what it is done to. The conversion says it, and
`teaching_sources._frame_places` says it of VerbNet's frames, so "NP:Agent V NP:Experiencer" gives the object
`done_to` as the PMB's meanings do. `on_store.py` takes several sets (`WORDS_TEST` separated by commas), reads each
document once and scores every set on its own, as (74) said it did.

**Taught** (lyric_dev2): the 18 words of the participle set it held no record of ("chained", "developed",
"thrilling", "broken", "interesting", "married", "crowded", "escaped", "orphaned", "riveting", "unarmed", "born",
"boiled", "depressing", "disgusting", "embarrassed", "exhausted", "left"), then "left-handed" and "hard-boiled", whose
gold is one hyphened adjective; and the 40 sentence records it holds whose gold meaning the Experiencer rule corrects,
built afresh (`record_of_pmb`) and corrected in place. None refused; no concept, belief or domain made.

**Found, not fixed.** A passive's subject. The PMB links it `done_to` 49% of the time and `done_by` 42% (678 of the
train documents' places), by the verb: a Patient for "injure" and "soak", a Theme alone — which the meaning language
reads as who does it — for "speak" and "elect". The reader says `done_to` whatever else is said, right 49% of the
time. The rule "done_to where a doer is said with it, else done_by", the meaning language's own convention for a lone
participant, scores 56.5%: built, measured, and taken out again, because it reads "Was the account locked?" as the
account locking something (`test_grammar.test_an_inverted_passive_question`) — the gold's split is the PMB's
annotation, not better English. The verb's frames, asked for the place as the active names it (a passive's subject the
verb's object), score 29.6%: asked so they answer for the Agent's place, not for the one affected. What would decide
it is the verb's own frame where one place alone is said. `verb_places.py` now prints each place's gold links and
counts both ways (`as the active`, `a doer said`).

**Measured** (lyric_dev2, all seven sets in one run, by their words with pronouns as unknowns; "before" is my run of
the six sets on the code and store of (77), 14:22 UTC, which reads them exactly as (77) records).

| by their words | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the 77 | 46 (F1 82.1%) | **49** (84.1%) |
| degree (20) | 12 (84.1%) | **13** (90.9%) |
| participle (18, new) | 2 of the 6 it then read | **9** (F1 76.1%) |
| denial (13) / hyphen (15) / kind of (10) / clock (9) | 6 / 6 / 5 / 6 | the same |

Four sentences became right and none became wrong: "Is the dog chained?", "Israel is a developed country.", "This is
so depressing." (the degree of a participle's quality), "I've been stung by a hornet.". "Riding a horse is really
thrilling." now reads the quality and its degree and misses one link: the horse, which the PMB's gold says the riding
is done by (its Theme alone) and Lyric reads as what it is done to. Main was not run again (the owner's word; its

Of the participle set's 9 left, one is a participle read wrong ("He is a born poet.": "born" read as the bearing it

at all ("It's a riveting story.", the sense having no name of its own).

**Where it stands.** The 77 by their words: lyric_dev2 49 (64%), main 40 (52%); the bar is 95%. Participles standing
where a quality may stand read as qualities where memory holds the word as an adjective, which is what the
measurement says decides them.

**The 77's 28 left, counted by cause** (this run, each sentence under the one thing that would have to change):

| | |
|---|---|
| a noun or name of several words | **6**: "disco music", "IKEA furniture" (the gold says IKEA makes it), "fist fighting", "European Constitution" and "prime minister" split into a kind, "Phobos and Deimos" after a colon |
| which link a word says | 5: a verb's place 3 ("Nobody called him." `received_by`, "Our bus collided with a truck." the Co-Theme, "Caesar falls" `done_to`), a possessive 1 ("Boeing's headquarters" `part_of`), a time with "at" 1 (the gold links nothing) |

## 2026-10-29 (77) — A verb's places by its frame: what each place says, by the places said with it, as VerbNet's frames say

**Objective.** The 77's remaining errors counted again by cause (lyric_dev2, 33 wrong): which link a verb's place says
was the largest group ("Nobody called him." `received_by`, "Our bus collided with a truck." `done_to`, "Our colleague's
mother passed away." `done_to`, "The chicken is pecking at Tom." `done_to`), then participles read as passives or
verbs (4), what a later word refers to (4), names of several words (5), single cases (13).

**Cause.** A verb's place was linked by the place alone (`learned["role"][(verb, slot)]`): its word's PropBank places
(function tags, `_PLACE_LINKS`) summed over all its senses, and what sentences taught said, whatever else was said with
it. The PMB's roles are VerbNet's (`--roles verbnet`; Boxer gives a verb's roles by the VerbNet frame its category is,
Bos 2008), and VerbNet says them by the frame: "pass away" `die-42.4-1` "NP:Patient V"; "peck" `chew-39.2-1` "NP V
PP-Conative" ("at" the Patient).

**Research first** (`GRAMMAR-01/diagnostics/verb_places.py`: each place of each verb of the PMB's 9,552 gold train
documents, named as the grammar names it, against the link the PMB's conversion gives its role):

| linked as the PMB links it | now | frames of the gold sense, else now | of WordNet's most used sense |
|---|---|---|---|
| subject (6,455) | 90.7% | 92.7% | 92.0% |
| object (3,639) | 80.8% | 86.5% | 85.4% |
| first of two objects (243) | 39.9% | 87.7% | 83.5% |
| after a preposition (2,121) | 12.3% | 45.1% (with the word's frames) | 37.7% |

By the place alone, whatever was said with it, VerbNet's frames did worse than now (objects 42.3%): the frame is the
unit. The word's frames over all its senses do worse than now for subject and objects (its senses disagree: "call" a
Topic, a Theme, a Recipient), better after a preposition. A class listing the word with no sense ("call" in
`initiate_communication-37.4.2-1`) given to each sense no class names cost objects 0.7 points; given only where no
class names any sense of the word ("pass away"), it is right.

**Built.** (1) The word record (`word_record_of`): each VerbNet frame with what each of its places says
(`_frame_places`: the role VerbNet gives it, linked as `pmb_meanings.HAPPENING_ROLES` links it, a Theme alone who does
it; VerbNet's `Initial_Location` and `Trajectory` the PMB's `Source` and `Path`), and each verb sense's VerbNet classes
(`verbnet_classes`). `WordRecord.frames_said`: each sense's frames (its classes' and those they are part of), and the
word's. (2) The grammar holds them (`Lexicon.frames_said`) and links a place by them (`Lexicon.framed`): of the frames
of the sense read (`sense_of`, now decided before the places are linked), those giving the most of the places said, the
fewest besides; after a preposition saying no time, else the word's frames; a tie goes to the link it had.
(3) **What sentences taught said of the very verb's place stands over its frames** (`Lexicon.taught_role`; the share of
the role table its word's PropBank places said is kept apart, `place_links`). Found in the first run: "Who did Maurice
Papon torture?" became Papon tortured, VerbNet's one class of "torture" being one of feelings (`amuse-31.1`,
"NP:Stimulus V NP:Experiencer"), where lyric_dev2 was taught "You tortured a prisoner."; and "She attends school at
night." lost its object (VerbNet's "attend" takes a Goal, `has_purpose`), where it was taught "How many people attended
the meeting?". Tests: a frame's places as the PMB links them; the frames held by sense, linked by, taken back; reading
by them, and a taught sentence standing over them.

**Taught** (lyric_dev2): every verb it held (187) recorded again with the frames, and the four verbs of several words
the sets' gold uses that it did not hold ("pass away", "go out", "pass up", "take off"): 152 corrected, 4 new, 35 the
same. Main holds no word records (its words were taught otherwise): its readings are unchanged, word for word.

**Measured** (all six sets, one run each; "before" is the code of c41ad563 in a worktree on the same store).

| by their words | lyric_dev2, old store | store taught | rule | main before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the 77 | 44 (F1 81.5%) | 45 (81.8%) | 46 (82.1%) | 40 (79.9%) | 40 (79.9%) |
| degree set (20) | 12 (78.4%) | 12 (84.1%) | 12 (84.1%) | 13 | 13 |
| hyphen / denial / kind of / clock | 6 / 6 / 5 / 6 | the same | the same | 4 / 4 / 6 / 5 | the same |

Teaching the store: "Our colleague's mother passed away." right ("pass away" held, its one place done to her), "He
passed up her offer." in its sense. The rule: "The chicken is pecking at Tom." right. Nothing right became wrong.
Changed and still wrong: "Our bus collided with a truck." (`done_with` to `done_by`: VerbNet's class of crashing has no
"with"; the PMB's annotators wrote a Co-Theme), "He came back at 5 o'clock." ("o'clock" still a thing, `moves_to`).

**Found, not fixed.** PropBank's `check.xml` and `rend.xml` (propbank-frames c66e0cc) are not well formed:
`word_record_of("check")` fails on them.

**Where it stands.** The 77 by their words: lyric_dev2 46 (60%), main 40 (52%); the bar is 95%. On the 9,552 train
documents the rule moves a verb's object from 80.8% to 85.4% to 86.5% (as the sense read is right); on the 77, one
sentence. Next: participles read as passives or verbs ("Is the dog chained?", "Israel is a developed country.",
"Riding a horse is really thrilling.", "I've been stung by a hornet.").

## 2026-10-29 (76) — Times of the clock: written as the treebanks write them, read as one time, their half of the day where the words say it

**Objective** (the last of the gaps counted by size). 13 dev documents say a time of the clock, 9 with a gold meaning
("I'll return at 6:30.", "We'll eat at six o'clock.", "The train departs at 7:15 a.m."). Neither store read one.

**Causes, from the root.** (1) The sentence's pieces: "o'clock" was "o" and a "'clock" that was its owner's (an
apostrophe began a piece before any letters, as before a clitic), "8:00" the number 8, a colon and 00; UD's EWT and GUM
write "o'clock" and "H:MM" one word each. (2) Reading had no time of several words. (3) The gold: the PMB's clock is of 24
hours, and its "07:15" was written bare (`7:15`) where the reader writes "7:15 a.m."; and the annotators chose the half
of the day no word says ("at six" 18:00, "awakened at five o'clock" 05:00).

**Built.** (1) `sentence_machine._spans`: an apostrophe begins a piece only before a word a treebank writes apart
(`_CLITICS`: s, d, m, t, ll, re, ve; "o'clock", "O'Brien" one word), and a colon between an hour and two digits joins
them. (2) `Lexicon._clock_time`: "6:30", "7:15 a.m.", "5 p.m.", "six o'clock" one time each, written as
`literals.classify_literal` writes times, its half of the day only where the words say it. (3) `pmb_meanings._date`: the
PMB's 24-hour clock written with its half of the day ("07:15" `7:15 a.m.`). (4) The measure, by their words: a time's
half of the day set aside where the sentence's words do not say it, as a word's sense is (strict and kinds aside keep
it). Tests: the pieces; the time of several words; the PMB's clock.

**Measured** (all six sets, one run each; lyric_dev2 taught the clock set's 9 untaught words, "Bob" and "Heather" left
out, names).

| by their words | lyric_dev2 before | after | main before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| clock set (9) | 0 (F1 49.4%) | 6 (91.8%) | 0 (41.1%) | 5 (81.0%) |
| the 77 | 43 (81.0%) | 44 (81.5%) | 40 (79.9%) | 40 (79.9%) |
| hyphen / degree / denial / kind of | 6 / 12 / 6 / 5 | the same | 4 / 13 / 4 / 6 | the same |

Nothing right became wrong. Still wrong: "He came back at 5 o'clock." (lyric_dev2) and "We'll eat at six o'clock." (main):
the time is read, but the structure view, weighing which word of it joins the doing, prefers "o'clock" a thing; "The
train departs at 7:15 a.m." (no future said); main's "I was awakened at five o'clock." (a state, the time lost), and
"The chicken is pecking at Tom." now `during(tom)` (wrong before, `located_in`).

**The gaps counted (71) are each met by a rule now.** On the 77, by their words: lyric_dev2 44 (57%), main 40 (52%);
the bar is 95%.

**Objective** (the next gap by size). "What kind of flowers do you like?", "I like this kind of apple.": the gold says the
thing a kind of the kind said, `isa(?v1, flower)`, no flower and no "kind" (the PMB writes "kind of" one line, `entity.n.01
InstanceOf`: "kind of", "kinds of", "sort of", "sorts of", 47 times; "type of" never). 10 dev documents with a gold
meaning, 30 training; "kind of" before a quality is a degree ("kind of creepy", 28), which reading had.

**Reading had** "kind" a noun and "of" a link: a kind and a flower, the one a kind of the other.

**Built.** The grammar's words "kind of", "kinds of", "sort of", "sorts of" before a noun (`N/N`, `subkind`): the thing is
written `isa(x, apple)`, never `instance_of`. **Found:** the entry was offered and never chosen: the structure view, from
UD where "kind" heads "kind of flowers", weighed "kind" joined to "flowers" as unlikely. A grammar word of several words
is joined as the grammar joins it, as a word that only marks another is (`_joined`). And a kind of a kind said of a thing
is no merging ("This is a kind of watermelon.": `equals`, as the PMB says it, never a watermelon). Test: a kind of a kind
the kind said, asked as a kind.

## 2026-10-29 (74) — Denials: a doing heads what a thing raised over it takes; what a thing is said not to be is denied with its qualities

**Objective** (the next gap by size). "Nobody", "nothing", "no one", "none", "no", "not a": 13 dev documents, 146
training. The gold says each as the lessons do: the doing is denied (`has_property(?v0, false)`), the one who did
nothing an unknown. Reading had the rule (`deny_arg`); on main most of these read right already.

**Found: the head of what a raised thing takes.** On lyric_dev2 "They suspected nothing." read "nothing" as a thing:
the words' own weights chose the grammar's "nothing" (-0.01 against -7.6 as a noun), but "suspected nothing", "nothing"
raised over the doing (`(S\NP)\((S\NP)/NP)`), was headed by "nothing", so "They" was weighed as joined to "nothing" and
lost 8.9. A raised word was headed so on main only because its tagger, learned from UD, calls "nothing" a pronoun
(`_joined`'s `_asking`); lyric_dev2's, learned from the PMB's sentences, does not. **Fixed by shape, not by tag**
(`_takes_its_head`, as CCGbank heads them, Hockenmaier and Steedman 2007): a function headed by what it takes, a
modifier (`X/X`) or a thing raised over what takes it (`S/(S\NP)`, `(S\NP)\((S\NP)/NP)`), in application and composition
alike. Also "who" raised over a question: "Who is John Lennon's wife?" now asks the wife.

**What a thing is said not to be.** "Edison was not a bright student." read Edison bright, the denial only on the kind.
The gold kept the student apart (`instance_of(?v0, student) & not has_property(?v0, bright)`): the conversion merges a
kind said of a thing with the thing ("Bergen is a Norwegian town.": 35 of 39 training meanings say such qualities of the
thing), but not under a negation, where a noun's line holds, so a separate student was said to exist. **Conversion**
(`pmb_meanings`): a thing said not to be a kind is denied with its qualities, said of the one it is said of (`not
isa(edison, student) & not has_property(edison, bright)`); its lines found once every line said to be one is (a role's
line is its person's). **Reader**: a denied "be" denies the qualities said within what it says the thing is. Two training
sentence records were built with the old conversion (lyric_dev2 holds them as they were). Tests: a raised "nothing" leaves
the doing the head; a denied predicate's quality denied; the conversion's.

**Measured** on all four sets in one run each (149 documents; the gold made by today's conversion for before and after
alike; lyric_dev2 taught the denial set's 17 untaught words first; before: the code of (73) in a worktree).

| by their words | lyric_dev2 before | after | main before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the 77 | 39 (F1 79.1%) | 42 (80.2%) | 38 (78.8%) | 39 (79.1%) |
| denial set (13) | 3 (63.9%) | 6 (72.1%) | 3 (63.4%) | 4 (65.0%) |
| hyphen set (15) | 6 (77.6%) | 6 (77.6%) | 4 (62.2%) | 4 (60.3%) |
| degree set (20) | 12 (78.4%) | 12 (78.4%) | 13 (83.9%) | 13 (83.1%) |

Gained (lyric_dev2): "They suspected nothing.", "Who is John Lennon's wife?", "Edison was not a bright student.",
"Nobody's taking a bath right now." ("bath right" no longer a thing); main: "Edison". Nothing right became wrong. Worse
though wrong before: main's "Wal-Mart has violated state regulations." now "has" as owning (the hyphen set's F1).
Still wrong in the denial set: "Nobody called him." (the gold's `received_by` for the one called, a verb's link), "None
of us will help you." (`member_of`), "No ship is unsinkable.".

**Next:** "kind of" (15), clock times (13).

## 2026-10-29 (72) — Words joined by hyphens: one word where memory holds it in some spelling, its words where it holds none; main never taught WordNet's 5,093

**Objective** (the next gap by size, 23 dev documents). What the PMB's gold makes of a word joined by hyphens, and a
rule that reads it so.

**What the gold says.** Of the 124 such words of its gold training meanings, 103 are one concept: a word WordNet holds
as written ("T-shirt", "man-made", "well-known"), with its parts together ("pick-up" `pickup`, "window-sills"
`windowsill`, "semi-final" `semifinal`) or apart ("roller-skate" `roller_skate`), a number ("twenty-seven", "five-thirty"
05:30), a name ("Ben-Hur"); 21 are their words ("ex-Senator", "13-year-old", "fashion-conscious"). Numbers and names
aside, WordNet holding the word in some spelling tells which: 57 of the 58 it holds are one word, 16 of the 22 it holds
in none are their words (dev: 12 of 14, 4 of 5). The misses are words WordNet holds under another name ("gas-hog",
`gas_guzzler`) and two the PMB splits though WordNet holds them ("ex-wife", "drug-trafficking").

**What reading did.** Two words around a hyphen were always made one word, named as written, whether memory held it or
not (so "novel-based" was a quality, `has_property(film, novel-based)`); three or more ("state-of-the-art") were
nothing, and the sentence was not read; and a record took WordNet's senses only as written, so "bullet-proof",
"ice-cream", "waste-water", "north-eastern", "button-hole" had none.

**Built.** `Lexicon.hyphened`: a run of words joined by hyphens, of any length, is one word where memory holds it in
some spelling (`Words.spelled`: as written, parts together, parts apart; `HeldWords.spelled` asks the sentences held,
the word classes memory holds and the forms), named by that spelling; where it holds none, the hyphens are marks and
the words are read as written apart. Numbers' and names' hyphens are read as before. `word_record_of` takes WordNet's
senses in every spelling ("bullet-proof": `bulletproof`, `armored bulletproof`, `incontestable unassailable`). Tests:
one word, four parts, and one held in no spelling read as its words; memory's spellings.

**The measure** counted a sentence's hyphened word as no word of it, so "by their words" could not set the sense of
"bullet-proof" aside. Its words now include each joined word in each spelling (`words_of_sentence`); every figure here
is scored by it, saved readings parsed back and scored again.

**Measured.** lyric_dev2 taught the words of the 25 dev documents with a hyphen (90, then the 16 hyphened ones the new
converter builds and "traffic"; none refused). Before and after on the same store (before: the last commit's code in a
worktree, its ignored data linked in; without `data/` its sense names differed and it scored 35 where it was 36).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| dev2, hyphen set (15 with gold): read whole | 12 | 15 |
| by their words, pronouns as unknowns | 4 (F1 56.7%) | 7 (80.0%) |
| kinds aside, pronouns as unknowns | 3 (63.0%) | 5 (81.3%) |
| dev2, the 77: by their words | 37 (77.3%) | 37 (77.7%) |
| kinds aside | 34 (78.2%) | 34 (78.6%) |
| main, hyphen set: by their words | 3 (53.6%) | 1 (59.7%) |
| main, the 77: by their words | 33 (73.7%) | 32 (73.0%) |

Gained on dev2: "We use really state-of-the-art equipment.", "I thanked her, and stuck the rose in my button-hole."
whole; "a novel-based film" now a basing, a film and a novel, as the gold. Still wrong: "bullet-proof" in the sense
`incontestable unassailable` (WordNet's first adjective sense of `bulletproof`; by their words the same word), "chocolate
ice-cream" (gold one concept, `chocolate_ice_cream`), "ex-con" and "ex-wife" (the gold's "ex-" is a time before now).

**Found: main holds no word joined by a hyphen.** Main got worse: "right-handed", "left-handed", "custom-made",
"hard-boiled" are now read as their words. Its 75,833 word classes told hold not one hyphened word ("bulletproof", yes):

letters joined by hyphens (85,372 words, 5,099 hyphened); main has them only once taught (`--source wordnet-classes`, a
write to lyric_db: his yes).

Also fixed: `test_wordnet_word_classes`' stand-in agent had no `recorded_name`, which `_held_name` asks since word
